Cam Ward is a playmaking quarterback from Miami. He has adequate size for the position and good athleticism. He is a gunslinger type of QB, with excellent arm strength, accuracy, and touch but poor decision making. He plays very upright in the pocket but still throws excellent passes and displays good pocket presence. As a processor, he can be a little bit slow as he often pre-determines who the ball is going to. He needs to go through his progressions a little faster. He has some good rushing ability, but it will not be his calling card. He is someone that can win games with his playmaking ability but may also lose some due to his decision making. He will be a starting QB in the NFL.
Anticipation – I’d like to se him throw with more anticipation, needs to predict better
Decision Making – He is a true gunslinger, makes some questionable decisions
Style – He plays in a very shotgun, 4 wide receiver, RPO style of offense that may not translate
Progressions – He sometimes seems to already know who he is going to before the snap, even if it’s a bad decision

Throw on the Run – He is excellent at throwing accurately on the run
Decision Making – He tends to be a good decision maker, on the conservative side
Spiral – He throws a very pretty, catchable ball
Processing – Seems to go through progressions well, is smart with the football

Shedeur Sanders is an accurate quarterback from Colorado. He has good size and adequate athleticism for the position. As a pocket passer, he does a great job putting the ball in locations where receivers can get YAC or make a play. He throws a very pretty ball and has a quick release. He has decent athleticism but doesn’t use it enough to escape sacks. He has good decision making but can work on throwing with more anticipation. His rushing ability is average at best, but he excels at throwing accurately on the run. His overall arm strength is average, but he gets the ball where it needs to go. Overall, he has an opportunity to be a very good quarterback in the NFL with his abilities.
Rushing Ability – He only has modest rushing ability, not an elite athlete
Arm Strength – He has subpar arm strength, not someone who can rocket the ball downfield
Pocket Presence – He does not have the strongest pocket presence
Escapability – Struggles to escape sacks
Anticipation – Can work on throwing with more anticipation

Quick Passes – He is very intentional with his accuracy on quick passes
Accuracy – He is a very accurate quarterback
Decision Making – He does a good job protecting the football
Touch – Has good touch on his passes
Escapability – He escapes pocket well

Will Howard is a solid quarterback from Ohio State. He is a national champion quarterback who can make accurate throws and limits putting the ball in harm’s way. He has excellent size and good athleticism for the position. He doesn’t have an elite arm talent, but he is very accurate and can throw on the move. He makes good decisions although going through progressions is a struggle for him. He can improve on his pocket presence and his overall playmaking ability. He has good mobility, although it is not elite. I really like his touch and his layering of throws as he can really put the ball anywhere. Overall, I think he will likely be a career backup who can keep a team in games if he plays.
Pocket Presence – Despite his size, he has a bit of a weak pocket presence, is not comfortable back there
Arm Strength – He doesn’t have a rocket of an arm, does not win with deep passes
Progressions – He takes a little while to go through his progressions
Ceiling – He is an older prospect who has not shined as a star
Elite tools – He is a jack of all trades master of none type player

Arm Angles – He can use different arm angles to make tough throws
Short Passes – He is very accurate on short passes and gets the ball out quickly
Rushing Ability – He has great rushing ability
Throw on the Run – He throws on the run with good accuracy and zip on the ball

Jaxson Dart is a talented quarterback from Ole Miss. He has good size and athleticism for the position. Dart plays in a very QB-friendly system with lots of RPOs and quick passes, which he has gotten very good at. He has a quick release with good arm strength and a multitude of arm angles. He can throw on the run and is decent at escaping the pocket. As a runner, he offers some good rushing ability. He can get you first downs if you need him to. His concerns come with his processing and ability to handle pressure, as a lot of his throws are predetermined and many times, he is under pressure, he struggles to make plays downfield. He can work on these things, but it will take time until he can be a starter.
Style – His offensive style is VERY rpo centered, which raises some concerns
Downfield Accuracy – He is not the most accurate player when throwing downfield
Decision Making – He seems to predetermine a lot of his throws
Progressions – Doesn’t go through progressions very quickly
Anticipation – He doesn’t throw with too much anticipation

Arm Strength – He has excellent arm strength, can launch the ball downfield
Rushing Ability – He is a dynamic runner, can get tons of yards on the ground
Playmaking – He is a player that makes a lot of special plays
Strength – Very strong play strength

Jalen Milroe is a raw quarterback prospect out of Alabama. He has adequate size for the position and has elite athleticism. He is a freak athlete with excellent strength. His best qualities are in the run game, where he is a dynamic threat who can run around or through people. In the passing game, he is very inconsistent. He has a rocket of an arm but has very poor accuracy, especially when it comes to anticipation. He doesn’t go through progressions well, as he like to pull the ball and run it instead. I’d like to see him protect the ball better, as he can be a wild decision maker. He also needs to play better in high pressure situations. Overall, he is a young player with lots of potential, but he needs time.
Accuracy – He is wildly inaccurate, misses routine throws often and doesn’t put his receivers in advantageous positions
Decision Making – He makes poor decisions with the football
Progressions – He is definitely a one read and run type of player
Anticipation – He is not especially amazing at anticipating routes
Sacks – Doesn’t feel pressure well

Touch – He throws with great touch on the football, layers his throws
Athleticism – He is a fantastic athlete who can move well
Arm Angles – he can throw with multiple arm angles
Throw on the Run – He has the ability to make accurate throws on the move

Quinn Ewers is a talented quarterback from Texas. He has adequate size and athleticism for the position. He has good arm talent, as he can use multiple arm angles and has good arm strength. His accuracy is hit and miss, as many other factors affect his throwing. He is very poor under pressure, as he takes lots of sacks and becomes inaccurate when there is pressure in his face. He is a good athlete who can use his mobility in the run game a little bit, but he needs to work on escaping the pocket more consistently. He can throw off platform and has good touch on his passes. I would like to see him improve with progressions and decision making as well. Overall, he has the talent to be a good player.
Pocket Presence – He has an extremely poor pocket presence, is very jittery
Progressions – He doesn’t go through progressions quick enough
Escapability – Takes way too many sacks
Accuracy – He is not extremely accurate on his passes
Pressure – He struggles in high pressure situations, does not have that it factor in him

body.text: Stability – Extremely resilient player, very difficult to take down
Speed – Breakaway speed
Breaking Tackles – Elite tackle breaker with many ways to beat them
Open Field – Decimates players in the open field
Vision – Very impressive vision, knows when to be patient and when to go
3-Down Ability – He is a willing blocker and has shown receiving ability

Ashton Jeanty is a special prospect from Boise State. He has decent size for the position. When I watch him, I think of a pinball, with the way he bounces off tackles and continues. He is an extremely resilient player who is a willing blocker and can be a 3-dwon back. He displays exceptional burst and speed, as well as a shiftiness that is untouchable. Perhaps his best trait is his contact balance, as he does not fall easily. He will be a broken tackle machine in the NFL. He displays impressive vision and patience when it is required. In the NFL, I would like to see him be more involved in the pass game.
Goal Line – He does not have the size that some RBs have which makes it difficult to punch it in on the goal line
Size – He is a smaller running back, which is not extremely concerning for me
Strength – He is an extremely strong runner
Toughness – Works through tackles with strong effort and toughness
Burst – When he sees a hole he can get through quickly and becomes a train on rails
Tackle Breaking – An expert at making people miss
3-Down Potential – He has good size and hands to become a 3-down back

Omarion Hampton is a big bruising back from UNC. A missed tackle generator, he has a unique bruising style of running. He is a downhill type of back who rarely spends time moving laterally. He has good burst and ability to find holes. He is extremely strong and has excellent balance. He has potential to be an elite 3-down back in an inside zone scheme. He has good hands, despite not being an experienced route runner. He has displayed good production, technique, and talent at UNC. I’d like to see him improve in his blocking. As a big back, he could be very useful if he improves in that area.
Route Running – He is not a dynamic route runner, mostly runs screens and checkdown routes
Blocking – He can work on his blocking technique
Top Speed – He is fast for his size, but he has potential to get caught on a long run
Bouncing Runs – He often commits to the inside run no matter what, despite holes opening on the outside
Patience – He has excellent patience; he waits and wiggles through small gaps
Balance – He has fantastic contact balance and stays strong and keeps his momentum well
Burst – He is very bursty, can accelerate quickly
Runs Hard – He runs extremely hard like he needs the yards
Vision – He has such incredible vision, always knows where to go

Kaleb Johnson is an incredibly talented breakout star for Iowa. He is a great-sized back who is very strong and compact. If you want to see a player with elite vision, watch Kaleb Johnson. He finds the gaps and wiggles through them with ease. He has fantastic balance and has the ability to make people miss. I love his burst and how hard he runs. He is not the fastest in terms of pure long speed, however he is difficult to take down once he gets going. In the receiving game, he is not involved enough with routes to show his true ability, but he has good hands and a bright future. He can be a 3-down back.
Power – He is not the most powerful guy, despite his size and balance
Blocking – He is not an amazing blocker, needs to work at that to become a better 3-down back
Speed – His top speed is not elite
Receiving – He has the traits to be a good receiver but needs to be more involved
Contact Balance – He has excellent contact balance; he stays up easily through tackles
Burst – He accelerates so quickly; he can get quick yards with ease
Vision – He has excellent vision, knows where gaps will open up
Strength – He is a tank, and he always falls forward
Receiving – He has significant receiving production; good hands

Cam Skattebo is a bulldozing back from Arizona State. He is in a compact frame, and he packs a punch. He has good vision in the backfield and his elite contact balance and strength allows him to always get positive yardage. He has good burst to shoot through gaps, but his top speed is lacking a little bit. He is not the shiftiest player, but he can make a few good cuts to create space for himself. In the receiving game, he is not very diverse in his route tree, but his production speaks for itself, with over 500 receiving yards in 2024. As a blocker, he has the frame and strength but needs to work on the technique.
Top Speed – He is not the fastest player in terms of top speed
Shiftiness – He is not the shiftiest player, more of a one cut and go type of player
Blocking – He can improve his blocking technique a little, can become more effective
Burst – Explosive runner with great acceleration and burst
Balance – Good contact balance as a runner, able to get out of arm tackles
Patience – He is a patient runner who will wait for holes to form
3-Down potential – He has shown willingness to block and some ability in the receiving game
Vision – Good ability to find the hole and burst through it

Quinshon Judkins is the feature back in a two headed backfield at OSU. Judkins displays a skillset that can one day become a 3-down skillset. He displays excellent vision and patience, and he is quick to burst through holes when he sees them open. He has potential as a receiver but needs more development and experience in that area. While he is bursty and fast, he is not the most explosive runner unless he gets into open space. He struggles to run between the tackles with efficiency. He displays good balance but not elite tackle breaking ability. He has a lot of good traits that will need to be developed.
Power Running – He is not incredible when running between the tackles, performs better in space
Route Running – He is not an experienced receiver, will need to expand his route tree
Scheme-Dependent – He needs to be in a scheme that will get him into space, not good at creating his own space
Bursty – He has excellent acceleration and can get going on a dime
Shifty – He is extremely shifty, moves very well laterally
Vision – He has great vision to find the open space on the field
Effort – Despite being small, he works his ass off attempting blocks
Receiving Upside – His skillset is good for a 3rd down back, he can catch and is quick with routes

TreVeyon Henderson is the second punch in a combo from Ohio State. Unlike Quinshon Judkins, he is not an elite tackle breaker and relies on quickness and lateral movement to win. He is an extremely bursty player with fantastic vision and high receiving upside. Henderson excels in open space, where he can move laterally or vertically and make people miss. He doesn’t have blazing, top-end speed, but he is quick and athletic. I love his effort, especially when blocking, as although he is a smaller guy, he works hard to hold his block. I like him as the lightning in a committee backfield in the NFL.
Power – He is not a run-down-the-middle type of back, needs to be in space to excel
Contact Balance – He is relatively easy to take down if you get a good grasp on him. Doesn’t stay up through lots of contact
Goal Line – He is not someone that will be able to win at the goal line, he is a smaller back
Patience/Vision – He has a perfect blend of patience and vision that he utilizes well
Blocking – He is asked to block quite a bit and does a good job
Explosiveness – He can hit a top speed quickly and be extremely explosive when he finds space
Tackle Breaking – He is excellent at breaking tackles, very good contact balance

Dylan Sampson is a stud running back from Tennessee. Winning SEC player of the year, he had an excellent 2024 season. Sampson has fantastic patience and vision as a runner. He can always find the gaps and he is an extremely explosive runner with elite speed and breakaway ability. He has excellent contact balance and is very strong in muddled situations. He does struggle with defenders in the backfield sometimes, and his change of direction is not elite. I love his willingness to block, he has the makings of a 3-down back. He needs to work on his ball security and receiving ability to truly become a star back.
Negative Plays – He does get caught up behind the line of scrimmage and has too many negative losses
Ball Security – He had 4 fumbles in 2024, which needs to be fixed up
Receiving – He is not a great receiving threat, needs to work on his hands
Change of Direction – He is not the most sudden player, occasionally struggles to quickly change directions
Explosive – He has explosive burst and speed; he can turn anything into a big play
Tackle Breaking – He is great at breaking tackles with his shiftiness and balance
Receiving Upside – I like his ability to run routes and catch the ball
Breakaway – He breaks big runs with consistency
Reliable – He is very reliable in almost every situation

RJ Harvey is an elusive running back from UCF. Harvey is a small but compact back, and he has a versatile skillset that offers good NFL potential. He is extremely explosive, with a 52.4 breakaway percentage on his runs, just behind Ashton Jeanty. He can break tackles in many ways, as he is shifty, quick, and he has good contact balance. He doesn’t have elite power or strength, and he struggles at blocking, but he can catch the ball fairly well. He is a productive back with two really good years under his belt. He has good vision and could be a really good runner in the NFL.
Strength – He is not the strongest running back, is not going to power through people
Blocking – He is a very poor blocker, doesn’t have good technique or strength
Too Patient – Occasionally he is too patient, and he loses yards
Size – He is a smaller running back
Shiftiness – He is extremely shifty in the open field, can make anyone miss
Vision – He has exceptional vision for the position, easily finds gaps and always seems to anticipate where they will be
Balance – He is very controlled in his movements and keeps his balance very well
Blocking – I love his willingness to block as a bigger back

DJ Giddens is an extremely talented runner from Kansas State. He is a young player with a lot of upside. He has excellent size for the position, but he can work on getting lower to generate more power. He has excellent vision in the backfield and is extremely elusive. I love his ability to make people miss in the open field. He is a very balanced player, despite not being the quickest or fastest. I like his effort as a blocker, and he can be solid in the receiving game if he works on his hands. He consistently falls forward and gains yards on almost every play. He can be a starter in the NFL in the future.
Burst – He does not have explosive burst to be able to fly through gaps
Hands – He has serious concerns about his hands, with 5 drops on just 32 targets in 2024
Speed – His top speed is not elite, is not a player that will beat u with blazing fast speed
Leverage – He is a bigger player, so I would like to see him get lower to win the leverage battle against defenders
Speed – Very fast top speed, long strider allows him to blaze past players
Size – He is a big back who could even add more size to his frame
Tackle Breaking – He is excellent at breaking tackles, many ways he can do it
Open Space – He is elite in open space
Hands – He has solid receiving production and secure hands

Ollie Gordon II is a talented runner from Oklahoma State. He is a very big back, with long legs and a strong upper body. A runner with low patience, he bursts through whatever is there initially. He has explosive speed and acceleration, and once he is in open space he is very difficult to take down. He was the most productive back of 2023, but his production declined in 2024. This may be due to other factors, but he did seem easier to take down and less twitchy in 2024. He can work on his blocking technique. With some more experience receiving and blocking, he has the potential to be an explosive back in the NFL.
Twitch – He doesn’t have the twitch and quickness that others do
Tall – He has long legs, which is a big target for tacklers
Blocking – He can improve his blocking technique
Patience – He is a very straightforward back, runs full speed at all times
Improvement – Had a better year in 2023 than 2024
Vision – He has great vision, finds holes in the line when there are none
Shifty – He has a low center of gravity and can move his whole body laterally very quickly
Contact Balance – He has good ability to stay up through poor tackles
Quickness – He is quick with everything he does, good footwork
Receiving Upside – Has good hands and can make things happen in space

Trevor Etienne is a well-rounded back from Georgia. He is a smaller back, but he has good overall athleticism for the position. As a downhill runner, he excels. He has great vision and a low center of gravity to keep upright through weak tackles. He doesn’t have great power but can make things happen in space. He isn’t the best accelerator but has solid speed and quickness. As a receiver, he has a lot of upside with good hands and good athleticism. He needs to improve his blocking and keep himself healthy and he can be a reliable 3rd down back for an NFL team.
Size – He is a smaller back, might not be able to carry a 3-down workload
Power – He doesn’t have a lot of power when he runs, relies on balance and shiftiness
Blocking – He is not much help in the blocking game, needs to improve on that aspect of his game
Durability – He has had injuries and hasn’t had a big workload in his career
Burst – He doesn’t have elite vertical burst
Receiving Ability – He is an excellent receiver out of the backfield, runs great routes and has good hands
Lateral Agility – He is very good at shifting side to side, has great agility
Speed – He is a very speedy player, can hit another gear
Smooth – He runs so smoothly, rarely ever is choppy
Vision – He has good vision and patience

Jaydon Blue is a speedy running back from Texas. He has average speed for the position but great athleticism. As a pure runner, he is not a bellcow or someone that will wow you with his power or contact balance. He actively avoids contact but is a very speedy player. He can break away at any time with good vision and a smooth running style. In the passing game he offers legit receiving ability. He needs to work on his blocking and his ball security, as he has 4 lost fumbles in his 200 carries. Overall, he is a shifty, athletic scat back who can have a role in the NFL, especially if he improves his blocking.
Power – He is not overly powerful, doesn’t run through people
Bellcow – He is not a bellcow running back, always plays in a committee
Ball Security – He has too many fumbles, needs to get better at holding onto the ball
Blocking – He is not a physical or strong blocker
Physicality – He is not as physical as I want my running back
Size – He has an excellent size profile, he is big and strong
Patience/Vision – He has a great blend of patience and vision
Getting Skinny – He does a great job at making himself skinny to make it through lanes
Contact Balance – He has excellent balance, takes a really good tackle to take him down
Lateral Agility – He has great agility laterally

Damien Martinez is a very solid runner from Miami. He played in a committee at Miami, and he played the role of the patient and tough runner. He has great size for the position, but he combines that with smooth movements and excellent agility. Martinez’s best trait is his vision and ability to stay up on weak tackles. He is also good at getting skinny to get through gaps. He needs to work on his receiving skills and his blocking if he wants to have a bigger role in the NFL. He has decent explosiveness but it’s nothing to write home about. He also does not have elite breakaway speed.
Burst – He lacks elite burst, does not have great acceleration
Top Speed – He is not someone that is going to break away with his amazing speed, is more of a patient back
Receiving Upside – He does not have great receiving upside
Blocking – Not a reliable blocker at the moment
Power – He doesn’t have amazing pure power for someone of his size
Elusive – He is extremely elusive and shifty. His movements are smooth and quick
Vision – He is a very patient and smart running back that finds the gaps
Blocking – I like the effort he gives in the blocking game
Control – He has excellent control of his speed and movement
Screen Passes – Is explosive with screens

Devin Neal is a smart running back from Kansas. He has great size for the position and is very athletic. He displays elite levels of elusiveness, where he is a smooth mover and makes people miss with cuts consistently. He has fantastic vision and is a very patient runner. He is not a power back, as his strength and contact balance can be worked on. I think he is less bursty and fast than some of the other backs, but he still is explosive. His role will likely be as a third down back due to his great blocking effort and ability to turn screen passes into explosive plays. He can work on his hands and route running, however.
Strength – He does not have the most power for a running back, struggles to fall forward
Contact Balance – He is liable to be taken down from arm tackles – Is not a great tackle breaker
Burst – He does not have the best acceleration, but it is sufficient
Hands – He does not have elite hands, would like to see him work on them
Shifty – He is an extremely sudden player, changes direction with the step of his foot
Ball Security – In his 4 years at Rutgers, he doesn’t have a single fumble
Burst – He is very bursty and quick, can get up field in a millisecond if the defense is not careful
Open Field – He can make people miss with ease
Effort – I like his blocking effort, despite his size

Kyle Monangai is a shifty runner from Rutgers. He is a very small back, which comes with his limitations, but he is very talented. He is extremely sudden and shifty. He can make people miss with ease. One of the things I love about him is his effort in the blocking game, as he always gives it his all. He also has exceptional ball security with 0 fumbles on 670 touches. He does not have a lot of power or ability to work through tackles. I would also like to see him improve his vision. As a receiver, he does not look bad, but the production is poor. If he works on that, I can see him carving out a role as a 3rd down back in the NFL.
Balance – He does not have the best contact balance; he is relatively easy to tackle if you make contact with him
Size – Immediately you notice that he is very small
Power – I wouldn’t trust him to get it on 4th and one or on the goal line
Vision – I don’t always think his vision is that great, misses gaps
Receiving – Doesn’t have production in pass game
Short-Area Quickness – He is very quick in spurts, can quickly pick up speed and change direction
Elusive – He is a very elusive running back, plays with slipperiness
Burst – He has elite burst and vertical quickness
Falls Forward – He typically falls forward
Center of Gravity – He runs low and keeps himself close to the ground, gaining leverage

Jordan James is a quick runner from Oregon. He is a smaller back who has a low center of gravity and plays with good leverage and quickness. He has excellent lateral agility and vertical burst as a runner. He can get through gaps with the snap of a finger and is talented at making people miss. He does not have a lot of power to his game and he can be taken down by tackles relatively easily. His vision is not elite and as a receiver he struggles. He needs to work on his hands and his overall strength, especially when blocking. He can be a backup runner in the NFL, with developmental potential.
Power – He is not the strongest back, is small and doesn’t play with a lot of power
Vision – He does not have exceptional vision
Receiving Skills – He has 5 drops this year, in addition to being unproductive in the pass game
Contact Balance – He is relatively easy to take down, not someone who is going to break multiple tackles on a run
Size – He has excellent size for a running back
Balance – Mullings has fantastic contact balance, can stay up through arm tackles with ease
Downhill Running – He can take hits and run up the middle successfully
Strength – He is extremely strong through tackles
Falls Forward – I love how he almost always falls forward

Kaleel Mullings is a late bloomer from Michigan. Not starting until his senior season, Mullings displays excellent size and ability to work through tackles, however he lacks experience and suddenness to his game. He has excellent strength and balance, and he falls forward on almost every play. I love his ability to break tackles. He does not have much nuance to his game, however. He lacks elite quickness and speed, as well as receiving capability. He has potential to be an early down back when you need to get tough yards, but he likely won’t get an opportunity without more experience.
Speed – His top speed is not very good, not an elite breakaway player
Inexperience – He only has one season with significant snap counts
Receiving – He does not get any work in the receiving game, a weak point
Blocking – He has poor blocking technique
Quickness – He is not very sudden, has poor acceleration and change of direction
Leverage – He does a really good job at winning with leverage
Strength – He is a very strong football player, can power through people and block
Blocking – Blocks his ass off, very strong player
Shiftiness – For his size, he is quite quick and shifty
Balance – He has a strong core and keeps his balance well

Tahj Brooks is a power runner from Texas Tech. He is a very productive runner who will make his money with his strength and toughness. He can run between the tackles very well, using his strength and solid shiftiness to make people miss. He consistently falls forward and can be trusted to get tough yards. He is not a very explosive player, as he has poor burst and underwhelming top end speed. I love the way he blocks, but if he wants to be a third down back, he needs to improve his explosiveness and receiving ability. He plays with great leverage and is a very strong player with a bright future.
Speed – He does not have top end speed; he is one of the slower runners
Vision – He does not have elite vision; I’d like to see him be more decisive
Explosive – He is not explosive; I would not trust him to make a breakaway run or big play
Receiving – He does not have much production in the passing game
Burst – He is extremely bursty, can get going in a flash
Shifty – Marks is a very slippery player, can make people miss in lots of ways
Speed – His top speed looks very fast on film
Receiving – He is a threat in the pass game, as he has good production and few drops
Open Field – He is excellent in the open field, makes moves

Woody Marks is a quick runner from USC. He is an older prospect, being a RS SR transfer from Mississippi St. He is a small back who plays in a scat back role, utilizing his receiving skills and his ability to dominate in open space with his shiftiness and quickness. He also has great long speed, once he breaks away. His weaknesses come as a pure runner. He does not have any power, and he cannot escape many tackles. His vision is ok at best, and he struggles as a blocker. He will need to improve his blocking to gain a role as a scat back/3rd down back in an NFL offense. He likely will be a late round pick.
Contact Balance – He has very poor contact balance, does not stay up on contact
Strength – He is not a very strong player, goes down easy and doesn’t get tough yards
Vision – He does not have elite vision for the position
Blocking – He is a very poor blocker
Size – He is a smaller running back
Blocking – He is a very tough blocker, plays hard and has solid strength
Shrugging off tackles – He is rarely affected by arm tackles, need to wrap him up to get him down
Strength – He is a very strong player, has a strong lower body
Size – He is a good size for an NFL running back
Downhill – Once he gets going, he can become a pinball bouncing off defenders

Jarquez Hunter is a tough running back from Auburn. Hunter may be the best blocking RB in the draft, as he thrives when he is asked to block. He displays his toughness and strength in the run game too, running with reckless abandon and shrugging off tackles left and right. He is not the quickest or most nimble player, and he does not have top tier explosiveness, but he certainly has a role somewhere in the NFL. His mix of blocking ability and strong downhill running will make some NFL team very happy. I would like to see him work on the receiving game to further expand his skillset.
Burst – He does not have very good burst, not a very quick accelerator and looks slow at times
Top Speed – He is a slower player, not going to be a burner in the open field
Shiftiness – He is not someone that will make people miss consistently with his agility
Receiving – He is not much of a receiving threat, bad hands
Balance – He has excellent core strength and balance, can stay up through tough situations
Quickness – He is quick, can get going and keep his speed up
Shifty – He is quite shifty and elusive, has good change of direction
Explosive – If you manufacture him touches, he can be a little explosive playmaker for you

Bhayshul Tuten is a quick runner from Virginia Tech. He displays great short area quickness and good contact balance as a runner. If he gets in the open field, he can be a really solid runner. The problem is he doesn’t get into the open field much, as he has poor vision, and he is unproductive in the receiving game. He can be shifty and explosive at times, but he lacks the consistency to be an NFL running back. He needs to work on his power and overall strength to have more of a role in the NFL. I likely see him bouncing around practice squads until he can carve out a role in some form in the NFL.
Receiving – He is abysmal in the receiving game, does not make the most of his targets
Power – He doesn’t have good strength in tough yardage situations
Vision – He does not seem to have elite vision, not great at finding holes
Role – Does he have a role in the NFL with his skillset?
Blocking – Not a great blocker
Size – He is a huge receiver, which gives him the advantage in almost every situation
Shiftiness – He is actually very strong after the catch, with shifty movements and quick feet
Hands – He always uses his hands, rarely body catches
Ball Tracking – He is elite at finding the ball in the air
Smart – He comes back to the ball and is smart when plays break down

Tetairoa McMillan is a stud receiver from Arizona. Brother of Bucs receiver Jalen McMillan, it runs in the family. He is a huge player, standing 6’5 with a huge wingspan. He is not an elite route runner, but he excels when the play breaks down. He does a good job at coming back to the ball and making people miss after the catch. His best trait is arguably his hands and huge catch radius. He is an excellent ball tracker which makes him a downfield threat. I wish he was a little more physical on his releases but that is something he can work on. He is a smart player with unexpected shiftiness for his size. He will be an elite WR1 in the NFL.
Route Running – He can be a bit of a clumsy route runner, mostly relies on size and athleticism to win routes
Physical – I want him to be more physical in his releases and catches
Separation – He is a good separator, but not an elite one
Reliable – He has extremely reliable hands, rarely drops the ball
Contested Catches – He has excellent ball skills and thrives with defenders near him
Feel – He has great feel against zone coverage to get open
Speed – He has sneaky speed, can take the top off
Route Running – He is a good route runner, especially in short situations

Emeka Egbuka is a reliable receiver from Ohio State. He has been a very consistent player for them, and in the right situation can be a reception machine. He has very strong hands with excellent ball skills and ability to catch through contact. As a route runner, he is very solid. He does struggle to separate against physical players, but he has an excellent feel for the openings in zone coverage. He is sneaky fast, but he is not great after the catch, as he is not the best at creating missed tackles. He needs to work on his physicality and strength to become a more complete receiver, but he definitely has a role in the slot in the NFL.
Physicality – He gets stuck with physical corners at times
Blocking – I’d like to see him show more effort and technique in the blocking game
YAC Ability – He is not special after the catch, is not an elite tackle breaker
Slot only – He plays almost exclusively the slot due to his struggles against physicality
Separation – Struggles to separate in man coverage
Three Levels – He can produce at all three levels on the field
Route Running – He is a very precise and creative route runner
Ball Tracking – He is an elite ball tracker who consistently finds the ball in the air
Contested Catches – He is excellent at making contested catches
Release – He has a very strong release package that allows him to create gaps of separation off the snap

Matthew Golden is a savvy receiver from Texas. Golden plays mostly outside receiver, which is where I project him to play in the NFL. He has an excellent release package to gain separation off the snap, and once he gets into his route, he is creative and precise. He is a menace against man coverage and has strong hands at the catch point. He can win at all three levels of the field. After the catch, he is not an elite player. He doesn’t have elite speed or ability to make people miss. I would like to see him show more effort in the blocking game. He also has some drop concerns, but his hands are mostly reliable. He will be a stud WR2 in the NFL.
Blocking – He needs to work heavily on his blocking, does not have good effort in that area
Speed – He does not have elite speed, does not breakaway after making the catch
YAC Ability – He is not elite after the catch, not the best at making people miss
Drops – He does have some drop issues in his three years in CFB
Size – For an outside receiver he is a little bit small
Speed – He has electric speed, can outrun most people on the field
Shiftiness – He has insane change of direction, skilled at juking people out
Hands – He has strong hands and goes to get the ball at its spot, doesn’t wait for it
Contact Balance – He has good contact balance
Versatility – He is very versatile, likely is a slot but can play anywhere as a receiver

Luther Burden III is an explosive receiver from Missouri. He displays a good, compact frame with excellent athleticism. His speed and agility are his best traits. He is a danger with the ball in his hands and can make anything happen at any time. He is a slot fade machine and is a dangerous deep threat with his mix of speed and hands. He  can separate with ease on deep passes but occasionally struggles separating on shorter routes. He is a good route runner but can work on his ability to attack the weaknesses in zones. I love his versatility and contact balance. He will be an excellent slot receiver for an NFL team.
Attacking Zone – He needs to be better at feeling zone coverages and finding the gaps in the zones
Consistency – He can be inconsistent, with games where he is not a factor at all
Separation – He is a good deep separator, but not an elite one in the medium/short range
Blocking – While he is a willing blocker, his technique needs to be better
Height – He has a big frame and can win with his size and length
YAC Ability – He has excellent ability to create yards after the catch, uses his body well
Route Running – He is a smooth and smart route runner, wins with head fakes and leverage
Hands – He has excellent hands, only one drop in 2024
Versatility – He is very versatile, has played both in the slot and outside for Illinois

Pat Bryant is an excellent receiver from Illinois. He has the versatility to play both inside and outside. He has an ok release package, but once he gets into his route he excels. He is a strong route runner who understands how to fake out defenders and beat them with technique. He has excellent hands at the catch point and can use his big frame to make contested catches in traffic. He is very good after the catch, as well. He does not have great speed, nor can he separate against fast corners as well as more physical corners. I think if he works on his blocking, he can be a very complete receiver and a number two option on a team.
Blocking – He struggles to block in the run game, does not show enough effort
Speed – He does not display elite long speed, cannot run away from defenders with ease
Production – He struggles to produce against good teams
Separation – He can struggle to separate on some occasions due to his lack of speed and elite explosiveness
Size – He has a huge frame, very tall and lanky
Feel – I love his special awareness to find spaces in zones and after the catch to know where defenders are
Hands – He has very reliable hands, only a 2.2% drop rate in 2024
Release – He has a good release package that can win in multiple ways
Leverage – Knows how to use leverage in his routes to win with his body

Jayden Higgins is a smooth receiver from Iowa State. He has a huge frame and a very lanky stature. As a route runner, he uses his body well, displaying knowledge of how to use leverage and spatial awareness to get open. He has extremely reliable hands at the catch point and can make things happen after the catch. As a big receiver, he needs to use his body more in contested situations, especially deep balls. Higgins struggles to separate on deep passes, and he shines most in the middle of the field. He can play outside in the NFL, as he has a very solid release package. I think he will be a developmental starter in the NFL.
Strides – He is a very long strider which hinders his agility and quickness
Separation – He is not the best separator, struggles to get separation on deep targets
Deep Passes – Oddly for his size, most of his success comes on short passes
Contested Catches – Is not bad at contested catches but I’d like to see him be more physical to try and win with his size
Size/Athleticism – He has excellent size paired with really good athleticism for his frame
Hands – He has extremely reliable hands, always catches with them and has a very low drop rate
Awareness – Uses leverage well and has good spatial awareness
Deep Threat – Bech has excellent deep skills, great ball tracking and good deep route running
Reliability – Reliable in every way

Jack Bech is a reliable receiver from TCU. Bech has good size for an outside receiver but offers versatility to play inside too. He is an athletic player with smooth route running skills and very good hands. He can make catches in contested areas and is solid after the catch. He uses leverage well and can be a deep threat with his ball skills and route running. He does lack elite speed and needs to improve his release package. As a separator, he just doesn’t have the speed to be elite, but he can separate on occasions. I project him as a big slot or a developmental z receiver in the NFL but think he can make an impact right away.
Production – Only has one year of really strong production, which is concerning
Speed – He does not have burner speed, can get caught on occasion
Release – He can improve his release against press coverage
Separation – Despite his good route running ability, his lack of speed makes it harder for him to create separation against man coverage
Separation – He can separate with ease at all three levels of the field
Speed – He has great speed and can be a deep threat with the way he can stretch the field
Ball Tracking – He does an excellent job at finding the ball in the air and using his hands to catch
Hands – He has very good hands, his drop percentage has decreased every year he has been at Iowa State

Jaylin Noel is a versatile receiver from Iowa State. He plays mostly in the slot but has played all over the field. He is a good separator who can win at all three levels of the field with his speed and athleticism. He is especially effective in the deep passing game where he demonstrates good ball tracking and the ability to make contested catches. He has reliable hands but after the catch he is not elite. He struggles with creating yards as he is not the most physical or agile player. He also needs to work on his route running and his blocking to make him a more complete receiver. He definitely has a role as a slot receiver in the NFL.
YAC Ability – He is not an elite tackle breaker and doesn’t make a lot of people miss
Physicality – Struggles at playing through physicality
Route Running – He is a raw route runner, does not display the level of detail and nuance that he needs to
Blocking – He is not an elite blocker, needs to work on his run blocking
Blocking – He looks for any chance he can get to put hands on a defender
Size/Athleticism – He has a unique blend of size and athleticism
Physicality – He plays a very physical brand of ball, very strong
Comes Back – Does a good job at coming back to the ball
Route Running – He is a creative and precise route runner, not an elite separator but still a strong route runner

Elic Ayomanor is a strong receiver from Stanford. He has an excellent, strong frame but needs to work on using his body better in the pass game. He has excellent athleticism, with good speed and quickness for his size. As a route runner, he is very solid. He is precise and creative; however, he is not an elite separator. He has solid hands, but concerns about drops are there. He is not elite after the catch, with only 3.9 YAC/Rec. His best trait is his blocking and physicality. He also comes back to the ball very well. He cannot beat press with consistency. In the NFL, I project him as a Z receiver in a run first scheme, where he can block and be physical.
Route Tree – He is not asked to run too many routes, needs to develop his route tree
Drops – Drops are a major problem, as he has an 8.7% drop rate in his career
YAC Ability – He does not get a lot of yards after the catch
Separation – He is not an elite separator at any level
Beating Press – He struggles against press coverage
Size – He is built in the mold of other Ole Miss stars like AJ Brown, big strong frame
Speed – He is a size/speed freak, has excellent long speed
Deep Separation – He is an extreme deep threat due to his ability to separate downfield
YAC Ability – He has promising YAC Ability, can break tackles and make people miss
Physicality – He is a very strong and physical player

Tre Harris is a productive receiver from Ole Miss. Harris is a big, physical receiver with excellent strides and speed. He has explosive vertical ability but is not very laterally quick. He is a deep threat who can make contested catches but does also have some concerning drops. He can make things happen after the catch if he gets the chance. As a route runner, he has a very limited route tree and is not the most creative or precise route runner. He displays a lack of effort when blocking in the run game and is not an overly QB-friendly player. He can beat press but needs more release packages for it to translate into the NFL.
Route Tree – Has an extremely limited route tree
Route Running – He is not a precise or creative route runner
Drops – He does have some concerning drops on plays that could be huge plays for his team
Non-QB-Friendly – He Does not improvise well and doesn’t come back on his routes
Ball Skills – He does not have the elite ball skills that a lot of other deep threats do have
Speed – He has breakaway speed, can be a real burner
Quickness – He changes direction on a dime, catches quick passes and gets upfield
Separation – He creates separation so easily, wins with quickness and technique
Catch and Run – Does a great job catching in stride
Release – He gets immediate separation with his releases

Kyle Williams is a speedy receiver from Washington State. He is a little small for the position but has room to fill out his frame. He is versatile in that he plays all over the field. He has a good release and his quickness off the line is extremely impressive. He has legit speed and can win vertically with it. At the catch point, he needs to work on catching in traffic and being more physical. On screens and quick passes, he does a good job at catching in stride to get maximum yards after the catch. He is not the most refined player but is very good at getting separation. Overall, he is a playmaker that will have a role in the NFL.
Size – He is a bit small and skinny for a receiver, will likely play slot or z receiver
Physicality – He is not the most physical receiver, needs to add some weight and mass to his body
Route Running – He is not an extreme route technician, can make his fakes better and cuts sharper
Catch Radius – He is not a big target, and he is not especially good at making contested catches
Agility – He is extremely agile, can change direction with the plant of his foot
Quickness – Has excellent short area quickness
Catching – He displays very good ball skills, sure hands and contested catch wins
Blocking Effort – Despite his stature, he blocks his ass off
Separation – He can separate effectively at all three levels on the field

Xavier Restrepo is a productive receiver from Miami. He has a smaller stature and plays the slot for the U. Restrepo is an easy separator at all three levels of the field with his agility and speed. He displays good ball skills and catches with his hands reliably. He can make lots of things happen after the catch and shows plus effort in the blocking game. He is not a very physical player and struggles against physical corners. He also is a raw route runner with some routes taking too long to develop and others being predictable. I love his ability to make contested catches despite his stature. He can be a starting slot receiver in the NFL.
Size – He is a smaller, skinnier player who can afford to add some weight
Top of Route – He can be a bit of a raw route runner, especially at the top of his route, needs to do a better job at separating there
Physicality – He struggles to play through more physical corners
Positional Versatility – He is not big enough or good enough against press to play anywhere other than the slot
Release – Has a strong release package
Separation – Does a good job at creating separation using athleticism and leverage
YAC Ability – He is good after the catch, has very good quickness and makes people miss
Height/Length – He is tall with long arms (good catch radius)
Route Running – He is a very strong route runner who can win at all three levels

Tai Felton is a versatile receiver from Maryland. He mostly lines up at the z but has played at the x and in the slot at Maryland. He has a solid release package and really knows how to win routes with savvy technique and agility. He has good height but needs to fill out his frame as he struggles with physicality and is not a very good blocker. He has solid hands, despite 8 drops in 2024, but he is not someone that is a consistent contested catch winner. After the catch he can make things happen, consistently making plays from screen passes. I think he has a role for any NFL team due to his versatile skillset and history.
Drops – Had 8 drops in 2024, a lot of them coming in the second half of the season
Physicality – He is a little light for his height, struggles against physical corners that get their hands on him
Blocking – He is a poor blocker, does not display the effort nor the technique required
Catch in Traffic – Consistently has about a 35-40% contested catch rate throughout his years at Maryland
Quickness – He is extremely quick on his feet
Speed – He has excellent long speed, can be a burner on deep routes
Route Running – He is a very precise route runner who can stop on a dime
YAC Ability – Many of his yards come from screen passes, where he is able to work in the open field
Separation – He excels at creating separation against man coverage

Isaiah Bond is a talented receiver from Texas. Bond plays mostly outside, but projects to more of a slot guy or a deep threat at the z position. Texas puts him in motion a lot, which helps utilize his quick and speedy skillset. He is a blazer with elite speed and excellent change of direction. He is a creative and precise route runner who does a good job at creating separation against man coverage. He can improve his ability to get open in zone, as well as his ability to make contested catches. He is very explosive after the catch and likely has a role in the NFL as a developmental firecracker who can get explosives.
Production – He has been held back by injury and stacked WR rooms, but his production has never been great in college
Contested Catches – Only has a 30% contested catch rate in his career
Feeling zones – Needs to be better against zone coverage and getting open
Blocking – He is not much help in the run game, would like to see more effort in that area
YAC Ability – He is excellent at creating yards after the catch with his quickness and shiftiness
Route Running – He is a precise and creative route runner
Hands – Doesn’t catch with his body
Release – I like his release package, can generate separation off the snap
Open Field – He excels off of screen passes and plays that get him in the open field

Jalen Royals is an explosive playmaker from Utah State. He is the type of player who you just need to get the ball in his hands, and he will do the rest. He has a solid release package but needs to be more wary of physical corners. He displays solid route running, especially on shorter routes, but he struggles to separate from physical corners. He has solid hands but is not elite in contested situations. After the catch is where he shines, as he is a slippery player to take down in the open field. I need to see him against better competition and with a less gimmicky offense to see more from him. In the NFL, he can be a developmental playmaker.
Blocking – He is little to no help in the run game, struggles to block
Route Tree – He plays in a very RPO centered offense, so his route tree is very limited
Physicality – He struggles to separate against physical corners
Competition Level – He does not play any elite defenses, needs to prove himself at a higher level
Size – He may have size concerns, looks smaller on the field
Release – He has a creative and quick release package to get separation off the line
Route Running – He is an excellent route runner who is precise with his cuts
Separation – He excels at creating separation on all three levels, can win deep, short, or mid-field
Athleticism – Good athlete, fast, jumps high
Versatility – Can play outside or inside at receiver

Kobe Hudson is a talented receiver from UCF. He is a versatile player who can play inside or outside as a receiver. He has a very good release package and excels at creating quick separation. He is a strong route runner with the ability to win at all three levels, and he is an excellent athlete to make almost any catch. He does have some drop concerns and physicality concerns at the catch point. After the catch, he is ok but not elite. He doesn’t have the tackle-breaking ability to be a big threat in that way. In college he suffered from bad QB play and an RPO-heavy offense, so I am interested to see how he translates to the NFL.
Hands – He does not have very reliable hands, consistently has a double digit drop rate
Route Tree – He is in a very gimmicky, RPO-heavy offense so he doesn’t get to run too many complex routes
YAC Ability – He is not an elite threat after the catch, not the most agile or able to break tackles
Play Strength – Needs to improve his physicality and play strength, struggles to win against contact
Measurables – He has a tall, lanky frame with good length and hand size
Leverage – He does a good job using leverage on his routes to create separation
Hands – He catches with his hands and has had a low drop rate
Deep Threat – He is a deep threat with his speed and contested catch ability
Ball Tracking – He is good at finding the ball in the air

Tory Horton is a lanky receiver from Colorado State. He has good height and length for the position. As a route runner, he needs to work on his release, and after that, I’d like to see him be smoother in his route running. He does play with solid leverage and quickness. At the catch point, he has good hands and has shown the ability to catch in traffic. He is a long strider, and a deep threat might be his role in the NFL. He needs to be much more physical, as he is a poor blocker, and he struggles with handsy corners. He did play against lower competition, so it may be an adjustment at the NFL level. He needs to develop and add some weight.
Blocking – He is a horrendous blocker, cannot move anyone
Physicality – He lacks elite physicality and toughness as a receiver, needs to be stronger
Route Running – He is not an extremely polished route runner, needs to be smoother
Route Tree – He plays in a relatively gimmicky offense at CSU
Release – Needs to work on his release package to be effective in the NFL
Short-Area Quickness – He has elite short area quickness, can accelerate in an instant
Agility – Super agile player, changes direction with ease
Route Running – He is a very precise route runner who can create separation
Feel – Does a good job at feeling where the gaps are in zone coverage
YAC Ability – He can make things happen after the catch, also avoids big hits

Tez Johnson is a speedy slot receiver from Oregon. Tez has elite movement skills, with excellent quickness and agility. He makes even the most athletic defenders look silly. He is a strong route runner with good feel in zone coverage. He has improved his hands each year, and he finished 2024 with just a 3.5% drop rate. He is extremely small for the position, and there will be concerns about health and longevity in the league. He also struggles when defenders get their hands on him, making him slot only. He has decent effort in the blocking game, but I’d like to see more. Overall he needs to add some weight to become a starter in the NFL.
Size – He is tiny and extremely light, concerns about health and longevity in the NFL will be there
Contested Catches – He is certainly not someone you want to throw the ball to when he is covered
Physicality – He is not the strongest, struggles against players that can get their hands on him
Blocking – He is a very poor blocker, does not have the technique or the strength to be consistent
Frame – He has an excellent, tall frame with long arms
Route Running – He is a precise route runner, makes good cuts and gets open
Production – Won the triple crown for receivers in 2024
Deep Threat – He can be a legit deep threat with his ability to get vertical and make contested catches
Hands – He has reliable hands that are very strong

Nick Nash is a productive receiver from SJSU. Winning the triple crown in 2024, he dominated opponents. The issue is that those opponents were not elite football schools. He plays slot receiver and there are concerns that he may be a slot-only player in the NFL. He is a good route runner and a legit deep threat with strong hands and a long frame. After the catch he is ok, but he is not overly dynamic. I would like to see him be more physical in his routes and beat man coverage with more consistency. As an NFL receiver, I could see him being a developmental big slot guy with legit deep threat ability, but he has some things he has to work on.
Slot only – Despite his size, he plays over 90% of his snaps in the slot
Competition Level – He has not played at a high competition level at SJSU
YAC Ability – He is not great after the catch, not an elite tackle breaker
Physicality – Struggles to beat physical corners that get their hands on him
Feel – He doesn’t have a great feel of where he should be or where the openings are in zone
Positional Versatility – He can line up at many different positions and win
Size – He has elite, big body size for the position
Contested Catches – He is elite in contested catch situations
Physicality – He is a physical player with a very strong build
YAC Ability – He can get yards after the catch with his size and speed

Savion Williams is a confusing watch from TCU. Williams has elite size for the position, and he uses his body well, especially in contested situations. What is confusing about him is that he has extremely strong hands and wins almost every contested situation, but also has tons of drops which should be routine catches. He has a solid release package and can make things happen in the open field. He struggles as a route runner and his pure agility is not great. He hasn’t had an overly productive season throughout his college career, and I expect he will need to develop at least a couple years before he does in the NFL
Route Tree – He has an extremely limited route tree
Drops – He has an extremely high drop rate at 11.8%, lots of concentration drops
Agility – His foot quickness is poor, has bad agility and can’t change direction quickly
Route Running – He is not a good route runner
Production – Has not had more than 650 yards receiving in his 5-year career at TCU
Size – He has excellent size for the position, great length and frame
Route Creativity – He is creative when running routes, good head fakes and footwork
Release – He has the ability to win against press coverage right away
Deep Threat – He does have the ability to stretch the field with his ability to win against man coverage and get downfield

Kaden Prather is a big target from Maryland. He has lots of positives but an equal amount of negatives in his game. He has an excellent frame and fantastic catch radius, but he struggles to consistently win contested matchups. He has a solid release and can stretch the field as a deep threat despite lacking elite speed. He doesn’t have an extremely diverse route tree and can look a little clunky when running. I do like his route creativity and think he can build on that to be a better separator. After the catch, he is ok but it is not his calling card. He will likely end up being a backup x receiver for an NFL team. He has some developing to do.
Body Catching – He does tend to catch the ball with his body on some occasions
Contested Catches – For his frame, I expect him to be better, but he is not great in contested situations
Route Tree – He does not have a diverse route tree
Separation – He struggles to separate against man coverage
Production – He has never had more than 700 yards in a season
Size/Athleticism – He is a big player but has excellent athleticism for the size
Versatility – He plays absolutely everywhere; he was their best player, and they knew it at PSU
YAC Ability – He is excellent after the catch, can win in multiple ways
Hands – He has very sure hands, catches everything
Playmaking – He is a true playmaker; he just makes plays

Tyler Warren is a playmaking tight end from Penn State. He has excellent size and athleticism for the position. He was used in so many ways at PSU that he can do almost everything for you. As a blocker, he displays good effort and decent functional strength, but he isn’t great at sustaining blocks. As a receiver, he excels. He is a vertical threat with his massive catch radius and sure hands through traffic, but his best quality is his ability after the catch. He can run through, around, or over players with his burst and tackle breaking ability. He isn’t a refined route runner or the fastest player, but he will make tons of plays for an NFL team.
Route Running – He is not an elite route runner, does not win with amazing change of direction or a big route tree
Speed – His overall top speed is not great
Blocking – While he is a willing blocker and has some good reps, he needs to be more consistent with sustaining blocks
Wacky Use – He was used in so many ways at PSU that he doesn’t have a lot of reps as a regular in-line TE
Height/Athleticism – He is a very tall player with great athleticism
Versatility – He can be used in lots of alignments including in-line, slot, or outside
Route Running – He is a very smooth route runner, creates separation
Hands – He has easy hands, catches everything
Vertical Threat – He can be an elite seam threat with his burst and speed

Colston Loveland is a talented receiving tight end from Michigan. He has good height for the position but could fill out his frame a little more and add some strength. He is a phenomenal athlete who has natural fluidity. As a route runner, he is excellent at creating separation and getting open. He has reliable hands and can make contested catches as well. After the catch, he is bursty and speedy and can win in many ways. He is a very versatile player. His only weakness comes with his blocking, as he is not a dynamic blocker and struggles with stronger players. Overall, he will be an absolute weapon for an NFL team.
Blocking – He is a willing blocker, but he struggles with technique and strength when sustaining blocks
Strength – His overall functional strength is not the best for a tight end
Position? – He plays mostly a slot-like role at Michigan
Route Running – He is a very savvy route runner, wins with good cuts and burst
Athleticism – He is an excellent athlete, has fantastic fluidity and good agility and speed
Hands – He had a 1.8% drop rate last year, reliable hands
Spatial Awareness – He is very good at sitting in zones and finding open space
Smooth – He is a very smooth player who wins with it

Mason Taylor is a dynamic chain-mover from LSU. He is the son of Dolphins legend Jason Taylor, although Mason plays tight end. He has adequate size and excellent athleticism for the position. As a receiver, he excels in zone coverage, where he can find space and make plays happen. He is a good route runner who runs so smoothly. He has great hands, with just one drop last year, and is above average after the catch. He doesn’t have a lot of production, but the talent is there. As a blocker, he is very willing to block and surprisingly decent, but his functional strength and technique can improve. He will be a starter in the NFL.
Production – He doesn’t have any season over 600 receiving yards, not a super productive player
Strength – His overall functional strength when blocking is a little bit subpar
Blocking Technique – He is a very willing blocker, but he often plays too high, and his hands are often wide
Size – He is a big tight end with good weight distribution
Blocking – He is a willing blocker who can hold his own against defenders
Contested Catches – He has strong hands and can high point the football well
Play Strength – He is strong through contact and doesn’t waver
Athleticism – He has good functional athleticism, bursty and strong

Mitchell Evans is a strong tight end from Notre Dame. He has excellent size and strength for the position, and he has good athleticism. He projects as an in-line tight end and that is what he mostly was at Notre Dame. He has a limited route tree and is not a polished route runner, but he gets open with physicality and burst. He has reliable hands and a big catch radius, and he is excellent in contested situations. After the catch he is not super dynamic as he isn’t shifty or fast. As a blocker, he displays good effort and is effective. He can clean his technique up, but he does better than most college tight ends. Overall, he has a role in the NFL and has potential.
Route Running – Not a super savvy route runner, his cuts are choppy and predictable
YAC Ability – He is not especially shifty after the catch, only 4.4 YAC/Rec
Production – He is not an overly productive tight end, never over 500 yards in a season
Route Tree – Very limited route tree
Dynamic – He is not an elite separator or dynamic with the ball in his hands
Versatility – He plays lots of inline tight end but also in the slot
Athleticism – He is a good athlete, fluid mover
Speed – He has good speed, can outrun linebackers and some safeties
YAC Ability – Averaged 9 YAC/Rec in 2024
Blocking – He shows good effort blocking and can be effective, especially when making moving blocks

Terrance Ferguson is a talented tight end from Oregon. He is not the biggest guy, as he is a little thin for the position, but he plays hard. He has excellent fluidity and speed for the position, which shows up when he is receiving. He is great after the catch, as he is shifty and quick. His route running needs some work, as it is a limited route tree and he is predictable. At the catch point, I’d like to see him be more physical and bring down more 50/50 balls. In the run game, he is a blocker that gives effort and is not bad, but his strength can be improved upon. Overall, I think he can be a good complimentary tight end but not a star in the league.
Strength – He doesn’t have elite functional strength, does not win with raw power
Hands – He had 4 drops in 2024, which is concerning
Contested catches – He is not someone who wins too many 50/50 balls, just a 36% win rate in his career
Route Running – He is not a smooth route runner, very predictable
Separation – Needs to work on creating more separation
Athleticism – He is an excellent athlete, very fluid and quick
Speed – He has good speed for a tight end, can outrun linebackers and some safeties
Hands – Only has one career drop, has good hands
Vertical Ability – He is an excellent seam threat, wins vertically often
YAC Ability – He can make things happen after the catch, very fluid and bursty

Elijah Arroyo is a fluid tight end from Miami. He is more of a big slot type of player rather than an in-line tight end. He is a little thin despite good height, but he is a freakish athlete. He is extremely fluid when running routes, his cuts are smooth as butter. His top trait is his ability to win vertically with his speed and catch radius. He will be a genuine seam threat for an NFL team. He is also pretty decent after the catch. As a blocker, he needs lots of work, as he often ends up on the ground. I don’t think he has the functional strength to be a good blocker just yet. Overall, he can be a dynamic tight end, but he is not a special player.
Production – He only has one year of decent production, less than 800 career yards
Blocking Technique – He is not a great blocker, often ends up on the ground
Strength – His overall functional strength is not great for the position
Role – I don’t think he has the size, strength, or experience to play inline tight end; he is more of a big slot
Thin – He could add some mass to his frame
Athleticism – He is an excellent athlete with good metrics
Hands – He has soft, easy hands; makes difficult catches routinely
Production – He is one of the most productive tight ends ever to play college football
Agility – He has quick feet and can change direction quickly
Vertical Ability – His ability as a seam threat is his best quality, wins vertically often

Harold Fannin Jr. is a productive tight end from Bowling Green. Fannin has less than ideal size for an NFL tight end, and his strength mirrors that, as he has to add some mass and strength to be an in-line tight end. As a blocker, his technique also needs to improve. As a receiver, he thrives, especially with vertical routes. He is very athletic and has good foot quickness, as well as soft, reliable hands. He can make catches in traffic and is decent after the catch with his burst. He can work on playing through contact while in a route, as he can be clamped on occasions. Overall, he has the potential to be a dynamic weapon in the NFL.
Size – He is a little small for a tight end, might have a different role in the NFL
Blocking Technique – His blocking technique is very poor, doesn’t set his feet and gets beaten lots
Strength – He lacks the functional strength to be a good blocker
Competition Level – Played at a lesser competition level
Contact – He can do better at playing through contact
Athleticism – He is a very athletic tight end, can do anything on the field
YAC Ability – He is excellent with the ball in his hands, can run through or around players
Hands – He has reliable hands, only two drops in his collegiate career
Red Zone – He is a true red zone threat with his height, wins jump balls
Zone Feel – Good at sitting in zones to get open

Gunnar Helm is a shifty tight end from Texas. He has decent height for the position but needs to add some mass and strength to his frame. He is a fantastic athlete, however. He doesn’t have a complicated route tree, but he does have excellent, reliable hands and an innate feel for zone coverage and where to be to get open. After the catch, he is shifty and plays with good effort. He doesn’t have breakaway speed or elite fluidity. As a blocker, he can hold his own sometimes but lacks the ability to sustain blocks due to his poor technique and lack of strength. Overall, he can be good in an h-back role for an NFL offense.
Size – He only ways 240 lbs, which is a little small for a tight end
Blocking – He is not an elite blocker, needs to work on his technique and be stronger
Strength – His overall strength is not elite
Separation – He is not an elite separator, does not have great speed or route running ability
Route Tree – He doesn’t run very complicated routes, mostly quick routes to get him the ball
Strength – He has incredible functional strength, strong upper and lower body
Balance – He has excellent balance, rarely ever loses it
Grip Strength – If he gets his hands on the defender, its over
Feet – Great feet movement in pass game
Pass Protection – Good against speed or power
Second Level – Good at taking on run blocks on the second level

Will Campbell is an extremely reliable tackle from LSU. He displays excellent size and adequate athleticism for the position. His arm length, however, is shorter than average. He may transition to guard in the NFL. As a pass blocker, he does a great job dealing with both speed and power. He has an excellent blend of strength, balance, and technique that allows him to stonewall players. As a run blocker, he is also good, especially on the second level. I love his grip strength and ability to stay in front of the defender. Overall, whether he transitions to guard or not, he will be a staple offensive lineman for an NFL team.
Length – He is under the threshold for NFL tackles arm length
Punch – He misses his punch sometimes, can be too far outside, would like to see a stronger, more consistent punch
Finishing – I’d like to see him be even more violent in the run game
Stance – His stance is very high, and he doesn’t get a big jump from it
Size – He is a huge tackle, with massive legs and a strong base
Run Blocking – He is a talented run blocker, uses good angles and wins with power
Strength – He has excellent strength, especially in his lower body
Feet – He has good, quick moving feet in pass protection
Balance – He always stays very balanced and square

Armand Membou is a big, strong tackle from Mizzou. He has a huge frame and excellent length for the position. He also pairs that with decent athleticism and light feet in pass pro. As a pass protector, he displays light feet, a strong base, and good balance. He does need to work on his hand placement and pad level, as he is susceptible to power rushes and rushers with lots of moves. As a run blocker, he is a people mover. I love his strength, but he can work on making blocks on the second level more consistently. He also needs to work on his timing in both the run and pass games. Overall, Membou can be a great guard or tackle in the NFL.
Mobility – He is not an athletic freak, can work on his mobility
Hand Placement – His hands can get a little bit wide and high sometimes, needs to keep them in the chest
Aggression – I would like to see him punch more violently
Timing – His timing is off on some blocks, mistimes the punch or the run block
Power Rushes – He plays too high, leaving him open to bull rushes
Size/Length – He is a huge player with excellent length for the position
Run Blocking – He is a people mover in the run game, does a good job at finishing his blocks
Feet – He is a smooth mover with light feet
Hand Placement – Gets his hands inside with a strong punch
Mobility – He is a very good mover
Power – Has excellent strength and power

Aireontae Ersery is a rock-solid tackle from Minnesota. He has an excellent frame with elite length and size. As a pass blocker, he has good feet with a strong punch inside. He does need to watch his outside hip, as speed rushers can beat him around the edge. He displays good strength and anchor to win against power. As a run blocker, he thrives. He is a smooth mover with vertical explosiveness. He can be indecisive at times about who to block, but when he has someone to block, they are always out of the way. He does a good job finishing his blocks. Overall, I think he is an immediate starting tackle in a zone run scheme.
Indecisive – He sometimes stands around trying to figure out who to block when he should be aggressive
Speed Rushes – He has to watch his outside hip, as he can get beat by bendier players
Pad Level – Tends to play a little too high on occasions
Leany – He can get a bit leany on occasions
Core Strength – Needs to stay square without turning body more often
Knee Bend – He gets good bend in his knees
Size/Length – He has ideal size and length for the position
Balance – He has a great base and very good balance when engaged
Athleticism – He has great mobility, very fluid mover
Feet – He has good footwork when engaged in a block
Hand Fighting – Does a good job with hand placement

Josh Simmons is a talented tackle prospect from Ohio State. He has ideal size and length for the position, and he pairs that with his fluid movements and athleticism. As a pass protector, he has a good jump off the snap and gets to his mark well. He has good hand placement and quick-moving feet when engaged. I do wish his punch was more powerful, however. As a run blocker he shows his athleticism but needs to be better at finishing blocks. He has a sky-high ceiling due to his size, athleticism, and technique, but I’d like to see him be more violent in every phase of the game. He can be a starting tackle in the NFL.
Run Blocking – He isn’t the best run blocker, misses reach blocks and second level blocks too often
Finishing – I would like to see him have more of a violent demeanor
Grip Strength – I wish he had a stronger grip on people
Injury – He suffered a knee injury in 2024 that teams will need to make sure is ok
Punch – His punch can be harder and more violent
Size/Length – He has excellent size and length for the position
Athleticism – He has good mobility, can get to second level
Hand Placement – He does a good job at getting his hands inside
Run Blocking – Does a good job at making second level blocks and displays good strength
Early Stages – Does a good job getting to his mark and engaging in pass blocking

Kelvin Banks Jr is a big, athletic tackle from Texas. He plays left tackle for them and has done a good job. He has great size and excellent athleticism for the position. In pass protection, he does a good job at getting to his mark and he generally has good hand placement when punching. He needs to move his feet more to generate better balance, as he is a very leany player. As a run blocker, he displays his excellent athleticism and strength and is quite good at opening lanes. I would like to see him be more violent, however. He also needs to watch his pad level, as he can punch high sometimes. He is a developmental tackle prospect.
Leany – He can lead too far forward on occasion, does not block with as much balance as you’d like
Feet – His feet are a little too slow-moving, often allows players to get around him
Pad Level – He plays with his hands too high on too many occasions
Grip Strength – Doesn’t seem to hold onto blocks for as long as he should
