Finishing – Would like to see him be even more violent
Mobility – He is a very agile player with excellent movement skills for someone of his size
Feet – He has excellent footwork while engaged, stays consistent and moves well
Quickness – He is very quick, can make reach blocks and pull blocks
Positioning – He gets in a good position off the snap
Punch – Has a solid punch against the defender in pass pro

Josh Conerly Jr is an athletic tackle from Oregon. Conerly has ideal size and length for the position, and he pairs that with excellent athletic ability. In pass protection, he has light feet and good quickness and positioning to get to his mark. His punches can be erratic but still solid and once engaged his footwork is excellent. He can get a bit leany and be beaten by speed or more talented rushers. In the run game, he displays good mobility to make reach blocks or second level blocks but needs to be better at finishing blocks. I’d also like to see him show more strength in his blocks. Overall, he is a developmental tackle that can work in a fast paced offense.
Hand Placement – His hands are all over the place, needs to get them more consistently inside
Power – He doesn’t have a lot of drive, especially in the run game
Finishing – Needs to finish run blocks better
Leany – Conerly can be very leany, needs to stay more upright and consistent
Grip Strength – I’d like to see him hold blocks, especially run blocks, for a longer period of time
Size/Length – He has great size and length for the position
Strength – He displays good strength, especially in his upper body
Hand Placement – Despite being tall, he does a good job at keeping his hands relatively low and inside
Run Blocking – He is good at opening lanes for the runner
Anchor – He has a strong anchor, does not give ground easily to power rushers

Ozzy Trapilo is a big, strong tackle from Boston College. He is very tall but has good weight distribution and good length for the position. He has adequate athleticism although I would like to see him get a little more agile. As a pass protector, he displays a strong anchor, good hand placement and strength, but needs to work on his feet and knee bend as he can get caught leaning or being too still and lose the rep. As a run blocker, he can make any block and does a good job opening lanes, but he needs to be more aggressive and move people rather than just getting in the way. Overall, he has potential to become a starter at some point in the league.
Feet – He has slow moving feet and often forgets to move them when engaged, needs to be more active
Finishing – He needs to finish run blocks better, doesn’t display great tenacity
Leany – He can get really leany at times
Sustaining Blocks – Needs to work on grip strength, occasionally struggles to sustain blocks
Knee Bend – Does not have great knee bend
Size – He is a huge player, very hard to get through
Second Level – He can make blocks on the second level
Smart – He recognizes blitzes well and blocks the immediate threat
Strength – He has excellent strength for the position
Run Blocking – He is a good run blocker, gets good vertical push
Grip Strength – Excellent grip strength

Cameron Williams is a raw tackle prospect from Texas. He has elite size and length for the position and his athleticism is very good for that size. As a pass protector, he struggles. He can’t get to his mark quickly enough to win against speed rushers, he doesn’t have great balance when engaged, and he has poor hand placement. He is very raw and needs some refining. As a run blocker, he is better. He is so strong and athletic that he can block almost anyone. He also gets good vertical movement. I like him to potentially shift to guard where he can utilize his skillset more. As a tackle, he needs lots of development, but his size gives him hope.
Feet – He has poor lateral movement skills, lets too many players get around him
Balance – He has poor balance; his feet are too slow to have good balance
Speed Rushes – Can’t get to his mark quick enough to seal off the outside
Hand Placement – His hand placement is often too far outside
Raw – He has good size and athleticism but poor technique
Finishing – He does a good job at finishing run blocks, doesn’t stop blocking until he has to
Punch – He has a very strong, inside punch that stuns the opponent
Run Blocking – He does a great job at using his body to open lanes
Strength – He has displays good functional strength, especially upper body
Tenacity – You can’t teach the kind of aggressiveness that he plays with

Wyatt Milum is a tenacious tackle from West Virginia. He has a tall, lean frame with solid length and average athleticism. As a pass blocker, he needs to work on a few things. Off the snap, his set is poor as he often either oversets or can’t get to his mark. He has a strong punch and good hand placement, but he plays high, and his balance is volatile. He has heavy feet and looks outmanned by talented pass rushers. As a run blocker, he is strong and tenacious. He finishes blocks well and can make reach blocks and blocks on the second level. Overall, he can be an asset in a heavy run scheme, but he will need to work on his pass pro.
Pad Level – He is a very tall, lean player who plays a little too high
Set – He doesn’t get to his mark quick enough and when he does, he gives up the inside shoulder
Feet – He is very heavy-footed and not quick with his feet
Balance – He ends up on the ground far too often, needs to keep upright
Knee Bend – Doesn’t have as good of knee bend as he needs to for the NFL
Athleticism – He is very athletic, moves very easily and can be explosive when he needs to be
Moving Blocks – He excels at reach blocks and second level blocks
Lateral Agility – He gets to his mark consistently, has good lateral movement
Body Control – He does a good job putting his body in the way
Balance – He has good balance when engaged, keeps head out of block

Charles Grant is an intriguing tackle from William & Mary. Grant has a tall, lanky frame with great arm length and good athleticism. In pass protection, he displays good lateral movement skills, long arms, and good balance. He doesn’t lean when he blocks and has a solid stab. His footwork and overall strength are a little spotty, however. In the run game, he is a smooth mover with good body control and ability to make any block. He isn’t a great finisher, however. Playing at W&M, he doesn’t have much film against premier competition, which creates an unknown in terms of how he can play against NFL talent.
Competition Level – He plays at William & Mary, does not have much film against competent competition
Upright – He plays very upright, needs to bend his knees more
Grip Strength – Sometimes struggles to keep blocks engaged for long periods of time
Strength – He is not overly dominant with his strength
Footwork – When engaged, his footwork is spotty
Size – He is a massive player, has a very big anchor and lower body
Foot Quickness – He has good quickness in his feet, moves them well
Lateral Movement – He is a good mover laterally, especially for his size
Strength – He is very strong, especially in the lower body
Length – He has very long arms, deals with powerful, long pass rushers well

Anthony Belton is a big tackle from NC State. He has a massive frame with a huge lower body and great length. He is an average athlete but has good lateral agility for his size. As a pass blocker, he has a lot of work to do. He has good burst to get to his mark but struggles with balance and hand placement when engaged in blocks. He does handle power decently due to his anchor and strength. As a run blocker, his hand placement and pad level is poor causing him to lose control. He needs to work on his knee bend to get lower and more leverage. Overall, he is a very developmental player who can potentially have a role later on.
Pad Level – He plays way too high all the time, loses the leverage battle
Hand Placement – He is a hugger when punching, his hands go out too far and he loses strength and control
Knee Bend – He does not have good bend in his knees
Balance – He tends to be leany and ends up on the ground too often
Athleticism – His pure athleticism is average at best
Size/Athleticism – He has excellent size for the position (with room to fill out his frame) and great athleticism
Knee Bend – He has excellent knee bend, can get very low
Versatility – Has experience at both tackle positions
Hands – He does a good job at hand fighting and striking first and strong
Square – Does a good job at staying square towards the defender, moves people

Grey Zabel is a versatile offensive lineman from North Dakota State. He has good size for the position, although he is a little tall, as well as fantastic mobility and athleticism. He is lacking in length, which is why he projects to an interior lineman. He has great knee bend for his height and plays with good pad level. Against the pass, he is patient and does a good job at hand fighting and staying square. Against the run, he displays good mobility and finishes well. He doesn’t have elite people-moving strength, but he does have good enough strength. Coming from NDSU, he played at a lower level of competition, but I believe he will succeed.
Strength – His pure strength is not one of his strong suits, does not win with overwhelming force
Competition Level – Played at NDSU, so the talent of pass rushers is lower
Length – He has underwhelming length
Run Game Hand Placement – His hands can be erratic in the run game, gets them too far outside or inside and has less control over the defender
Size/Athleticism – He has a good frame and great athleticism for his size
Mobility – He has excellent mobility to get to the second level
IQ – He passes off assignments and takes on stunts with ease
Strength – He displays good functional strength
Anchor – He has a good base and gives ground slowly
Hips – Does well creating lanes

Tate Ratledge is a strong guard from Georgia. He is a tall player who can fill out his frame a little bit but has excellent athleticism. Ratledge, being tall, needs to work on his knee bend so he can win the leverage battle more consistently. In pass pro, he has a good anchor, good IQ, and good grip strength to give ground slowly. He can work on his hand placement, as his hands are often wide. In the run game, he has great mobility to get to the second level, and he displays good hips and ability to create lanes with power or finesse. Overall, he has some concerns (especially with injuries and versatility) but he will be good.
Pad Level – He is a taller player and doesn’t have great knee bend, plays too high
Hand Placement – His hands are consistently too wide, causing “hugging” which can cause penalties
Versatility – Has only played right guard in college
Leany – He can be too leany in pass protection, loses balance
Injury – Has had two significant lower body injuries in college
Versatility – He played guard throughout his career, but had to play tackle this year and did very well
Strength – He displays excellent functional strength
Second Level – He is excellent at executing blocks on the second level
Finishing – Generally does a good job finishing strongly
Pull Blocks – He is excellent at pulling, very mobile

Donovan Jackson is a talented lineman from Ohio State. He played mostly guard at OSU, but he does have some tackle experience. He has a thick, compact frame with decent length and athleticism. As a run blocker, he does well in a scheme that allows him to move around. He is excellent at pulling and making blocks on the second level, and he finishes them with tenacity. He is strong but his anchor can be put into question at times. As a pass blocker, he can be leany and lose balance. His feet and hips need to be cleaned up, but he shows good hand placement and strength. Overall, he will be a starting lineman in the NFL.
Balance – He can be a very leany player, leans way too far forward when pass blocking
Hips – He can open up his hips sometimes, creating space for the defenders to work
Feet – His feet can be a little sloppy, leading to missed assignments
Recovery – He struggles to recover if he is initially beaten, needs to work on resetting himself and getting into a good position
Size/Athleticism – He is a very big player, who has surprisingly decent athleticism for his size
Strength – He has excellent functional strength
Run Blocking – He uses his hips excellently to open up lanes for the runner
Pad Level – He keeps his pad level low to win the leverage battle
Hand Placement – Keep his hands inside and tight

Luke Kandra is an experienced guard from Cincinnati. He has a thick, wide frame with excellent size and adequate athleticism. As a pass protector, he displays good functional strength and good hand placement, as well as the ability to take on stunts and find free rushers. He can be a little bit leany at times, which he needs to fix up. In the run game, he has great hips to swivel to seal off lanes for the runner. He does not have elite ability to make reach blocks or second level blocks. He can work on his finishing as I’d like to see him put more people in the ground. Overall, I believe he will be a durable starter for years to come in the NFL.
Mobility – His mobility is limited as he can struggle to get to the second level in time
Leany – He can be a bit leany in pass protection, needs to keep his balance better
Grip Strength – He doesn’t always hold blocks for as long as I would like
Versatility – He has really only played right guard throughout his college career, giving some question to his versatility
Size – He is a mammoth of a man on the interior, big enough to handle large DTs
Strength – He has excellent strength in both his upper and lower body
Tenacity – Plays through the whistle on every single rep
Anchor – He has an excellent anchor, gives ground very slowly
Hand Placement – He gets his hands low and inside to gain leverage

Tyler Booker is a solid guard from Alabama. He has excellent size and length for the position, but his athleticism is below par. As a pass blocker, he has excellent hand placement, inside and low, and a great anchor to win reps. He displays excellent functional strength and football IQ to stop stunts. In the run game, he is great on power runs. He is a very tenacious player who plays through the whistle. He struggles when blocking on the second level, as he doesn’t have the athleticism to consistently get there on time. Overall, he is not a scheme versatile player, but in a power scheme he has starting quality.
Athleticism – His overall athleticism is lacking compared to other guards
Second Level Blocks – Struggles to execute blocks on the second level
Versatility – He is not very scheme versatile due to his lack of athleticism
Feet – His feet can be clunky and slow at times, needs to clean them up
Athleticism – He is an excellent athlete, a smooth mover, and a quick reactor
Second Level – He does a good job at executing blocks on the second level
Pass Protection – He has a good base and anchor and doesn’t allow defender through
Hand Placement – He gets his hands inside and tight to gain leverage
Feet – Good, quick feet

Jared Wilson is an athletic center from Georgia. He is a good size and has a good base for a center. As a pass protector, he does a decent job. He has good, quick feet to get set quickly and displays good inside hand placement to gain leverage. His length is subpar, which creates overextensions occasionally. As a run blocker, he needs a little more work. He has excellent mobility to climb to the second level, but he struggles to find blocks there that are meaningful. He often is caught in a position where there is no one to block. He doesn’t have raw, people-moving strength, either. Overall, he can grow into a starting center in the NFL.
Power – His pure power is questionable, he is not a huge people-mover
Opening Lanes – He needs to use his hips better to open up lanes for the runner
Finding Blocks – He sometimes doesn’t know where to be and doesn’t block anyone
Tenacity – He is not super aggressive
Length – He has poor length, which causes him to occasionally overextend and lose positioning
Size – He is a massive player with a good base and good length
Versatility – He played both tackle positions and guard
Hands – He has a strong grip and has decent hand placement, can get a little high
Moving Blocks – He is decent in the run game at making blocks on the second level
Power – When moving vertically, he displays good strength and drive in his blocks

Jonah Savaiinaea is a versatile lineman from Arizona. Jonah has a very thick, built frame with strong arms and adequate athleticism. He plays all over the line, playing left and right tackle in 2024, but he projects as a guard in the NFL. In the run game, he is decent at making moving blocks, and when moving vertically, he displays power and finishing. He can get a little high on his pad level, however. As a pass protector, his poor lateral agility and poor anchor show up too often. He gets pushed back due to poor positioning and body control. Overall, he has a lot to work on if he wants to be a starter in the league.
Tenacity – He is not someone who finishes with consistency, needs to be more tenacious
Balance – He keeps his knees too far forward, is susceptible to being pushed back
Lateral Agility – He is not a great lateral mover
Anchor – He doesn’t have an elite anchor, can be knocked back
Positioning – He often doesn’t get himself in advantageous positions, loses reps due to it
Experience – He has played 5 years at center, 4 at Alabama
Explosiveness – He is quick off the line, has a very explosive start
Mobility – He is very quick on his feet, can get to the second level
Pass Protection – He is a patient pass protector who excels in help blocks and IQ
Moving Blocks – He does an excellent job making reach blocks and second level blocks

Seth McLaughlin is an athletic center from Ohio State. He is experienced, playing over 2,300 snaps in his career. He has adequate size but short and stubby arms for the position. As a pass blocker, his length can be a problem occasionally, but he does a good job staying patient and striking at the right time. He doesn’t have elite raw strength, but his technique is very good. In the run game, he displays good athleticism to make reach blocks and second level blocks, but his overall power is lacking. He tore his Achilles in November which will cause him to drop but eventually he has starter potential in the NFL.
Injury – He tore his Achilles at the end of the year, meaning the start of next year he will still be injured
Power – He doesn’t have elite people-moving power
Length – Does not have great length
Pad Level – He plays too high on occasions, losing leverage
Size/Athleticism – He has great size and very good athleticism for his size
Mobility – He has good mobility, as he reaches the second level easily
Pass Protection – He is a patient, good pass blocker who gives ground slowly
Moving Blocks – Does well on the second level and when pulling
Experience – He is a very durable player with lots of experience

Connor Colby is an experienced guard from Iowa. He has a lot of experience, and it shows, as he displays good football IQ and knowledge of his blocking assignments. He has good size and athleticism for the position. As a pass blocker, he is patient and has good hand placement and feet. He can get off balance occasionally and he struggles with oversetting. As a run blocker, he is very mobile and excels on the second level and with pull blocks. He lacks elite power and strength, however. Overall, he needs to improve on his power and strength in order to have a shot at starting, but he has a good foundation with his athleticism and pass blocking.
Pad Level – His hands can get a little high at times, causing him to lose leverage
Power – He does not have a lot of drive and power behind him
Strength – His overall strength is not as good as some others
Oversetting – He often oversets and loses reps and leverage
Balance – He is a bit of a lunger, tends to lean into his blocks which causes balance issues
Explosive – He is explosive in his movements, very quick vertically and laterally
Mobility – Can get to the second level and make pull blocks with ease
Finishing – He does a good job at finishing run blocks, is a people mover in the run game
Punch – His initial punch is quick and explosive, although erratic
Aggression – He consistently plays with high effort, always looking to block

Marcus Mbow is an aggressive tackle from Purdue. Mbow has a decent frame, but needs to fill it out a bit more, with ok length. He is an excellent athlete with explosive movements vertically and laterally. As a pass blocker, he has a lot of work to do. He does a good job getting to his mark and has a quick, aggressive punch, but his hand placement is often terrible, and he often loses his balance or footing when blocking. As a run blocker, he is able to make any block with his superior mobility and effort, but I’d like to see him be more consistent against lineman. Overall, he likely will be a better guard than tackle in the NFL.
Size – He is a little bit lean for a tackle, can add some weight
Hand Placement – His hand placement is very erratic, often grabs the back of players
Balance – He is a very leany player, needs to stay more consistently upright
Erratic – He is a jumpy player, falls easily for pass rush moves
Strength – He doesn’t have an elite anchor or great strength
Explosive – He is explosive in his movements, very quick vertically and laterally
Mobility – Can get to the second level and make pull blocks with ease
Finishing – He does a good job at finishing run blocks, is a people mover in the run game
Punch – His initial punch is quick and explosive, although erratic
Aggression – He consistently plays with high effort, always looking to block

Marcus Mbow is an aggressive tackle from Purdue. Mbow has a decent frame, but needs to fill it out a bit more, with ok length. He is an excellent athlete with explosive movements vertically and laterally. As a pass blocker, he has a lot of work to do. He does a good job getting to his mark and has a quick, aggressive punch, but his hand placement is often terrible, and he often loses his balance or footing when blocking. As a run blocker, he is able to make any block with his superior mobility and effort, but I’d like to see him be more consistent against lineman. Overall, he has a lot of work to do in order to be a starter in the NFL.
Size – He is a little bit lean for a tackle, can add some weight
Hand Placement – His hand placement is very erratic, often grabs the back of players
Balance – He is a very leany player, needs to stay more consistently upright
Erratic – He is a jumpy player, falls easily for pass rush moves
Strength – He doesn’t have an elite anchor or great strength
Mobility – He has excellent movement skills, can make reach blocks and second level blocks with ease
Leverage – He has the natural leverage on other players
Feet – He has excellent feet, keeps them moving at all times
Hand Placement – Does a great job to get his hands tight and inside to gain leverage
Tenacity – He plays with elite effort on every single play

Willie Lampkin is a unique guard from UNC. Lampkin is extremely small, at just 5’11, 279. His unique size makes him hard to project in the NFL. What is visible on tape, however, is excellent. He plays with great natural leverage, has excellent mobility, and great technique. In pass protection, he has fantastic footwork and hand placement. He can get off balance at times, but it is not a huge problem. He also plays with better strength than his size suggests. In the run game, he is fantastic at making moving blocks such as reach blocks, and he displays good tenacity. Overall, he will have to overcome odds but I believe he can be a starter.
Size – He is one of the smallest interior lineman ever recorded, gives major concern for his projection
Power – He doesn’t have quite the amount of vertical drive that others do, needs to get more movement
Quick Set – I noticed at the senior bowl that he always does the same move, which is a quick set punch with the right hand
Balance – Can get thrown around when he overextends
Leverage – He plays very low to the ground, which allows him to win the leverage battle
Two-Gapping – He is a master of two-gapping, can control offensive lineman at will
Strength – Exceptional functional strength
Pass Rush Upside – He has lots of pass rush upside due to his athleticism and talent
Disruption – He is so disruptive in both the run game and the pass game

Mason Graham is an elite disruptor from Michigan. He has a decent size profile, although on the smaller side with shorter arms, and he has great athleticism. As a pass rusher, he utilizes a swipe move and consistently wins laterally. He has the ability to win vertically but I want to see him do it more often. As a run defender he is extremely strong and sound. He is an excellent two gapper and seems to control lineman at will. He has excellent strength and can withstand double teams, and he makes plays consistently. He has good pass rush upside and overall, he can be the next elite defensive tackle in the NFL.
Size – He is on the smaller side, but it is not concerning due to his strength
Vertical Explosion Usage – He is elite laterally, but I’d like to see him incorporate more bull rush and vertical moves
Length – He does not have especially long arms
Explosive – He is a very explosive player, has lots of pop in his hands
First Step – He has a very quick first step, gets off the line really quick
Strength – He can really hold his ground against anyone
Versatility – He lines up all over the defensive line and wins
Disruptive – He does a great job at getting into the backfield
Leverage – + pad level

Derrick Harmon is an explosive defensive lineman from Oregon. He displays excellent quickness with his first step and has lots of pop in his hands at the point of contact. He has good size for a DT and is very versatile. He has played all over the defensive line. I love his upside as a pass rusher, as he has very good leverage and athleticism. Against the run, he is very disruptive. He does a good job at getting in the backfield but needs to be more consistent with his tackling. He also misses his gaps sometimes and he doesn’t have an elite anchor to take on double teams. Overall, he has elite potential, and I think he will be a star in the NFL.
Pass Rush Moves – He is a raw pass rusher, does not have a lot of moves in his arsenal
Tackling – His main issues come with finishing, especially tackles near the edge of his tackling range
Run Gaps – He occasionally misses his run gaps, needs to be better at two gapping
Double Teams – He is not elite at taking on double teams
Size – He is a huge player, consistently one of the biggest players on the field
Power – He has an excellent bull rush and some serious power behind him
Hands – He has good hand placement and does a good job at winning with his hands
Strength – He is a very strong player, especially in the upper body
Athleticism – For his size, he has incredible athleticism

Darius Alexander is a freak from Toledo. He is a huge player who has elite explosiveness and strength. As a run defender, he is very good. He has great hand placement and leverage and can shed blocks with ease. He also is a good tackler. He sometimes can get pushed out of his gaps, but it is only if he is double teamed. As a pass rusher, he has an excellent bull rush, but I’d like to see him rush with more of a plan. Overall, he is a powerful, explosive player with great hand placement and alignment versatility. He is 25 years old, which is a little old, but his skillset screams top 50 player. I think he can be an every down 3-tech in the NFL.
Get-Off – He doesn’t have a super quick get off, needs to time the snap better
Age – He will be 25 when drafted, which will turn some teams off of him
Pass Rush Plan – While he has a strong bull rush, I’d like to see him expand to win in other ways
Gap Filling – He does occasionally get knocked out of his gap
Explosiveness – He is extremely explosive, bursts off the snap with speed
Pass Rush Upside – He has elite vertical motion and can win in many ways
Leverage – He can get low and win the leverage battle
Power – He has lots of drive and power in his game
First Step – He has an elite first step and is very quick with both his feet and his hands

Walter Nolen is a raw and talented defensive tackle from Ole Miss. Nolen has good size for the position and average length. He displays elite first step quickness and great lateral and vertical mobility. He is explosive and powerful against the pass. He has a good bull rush and can be an effective pass rusher. Against the run, he occasionally struggles to hold his ground, especially against double teams. He can be a little slow reading and reacting to run plays as well. I’d like to see him be more violent with his hands and be a better block shedder. All in all, I believe Nolen has the skills and potential to be a great DT.
Anchor – He can be moved in the run game, especially against double teams
Lateral Strength – Whenever he does get moved, it is almost always laterally
Read/React – He is a little slower reading run plays, especially option plays
Block Shedding – He doesn’t shed blocks with too much ease, can be thrown around
Length – He has shorter arms for the position
Two-Gapping – He is a master two-gapper, controls offensive lineman and makes plays
Block Shedding – He is an excellent shedder of blocks, uses strength and length
Strength – Very strong player, stays square
Hands – He has excellent hand counters and hand placement
Agility – He is very agile for his size, can make people miss with quickness

Tyleik Williams is a strong defensive tackle from Ohio State. He plays as a 3-tech and is a run defending specialist. He has great size for the position and great agility to go with his size. I would like to see him be more explosive vertically. As a pass rusher, he needs a little work. He doesn’t have the explosiveness to consistently win as a pass rusher. As a run defender, however, he may be the best in the class bar Mason Graham. He has excellent hand placement and uses his length to two-gap and block shed with ease. He makes plays and wins with strength. Overall, he has an immediate role in the NFL with even higher potential.
Explosiveness – He does not have elite vertical explosiveness
Pass Rush – He does not have a lot of pass rush talent, usually focuses on the run, needs to gain more confidence in that area
Double-Teams – He doesn’t survive double teams very well
Bull Rush – He doesn’t have a great bull rush, seems to lack something
Size/Athleticism – He has a unique blend of size and athleticism
Length – He has extremely long arms
Strength – He displays excellent strength and power, especially in bull rushes
Movement – He is very agile for someone his size, especially laterally
Swim Move – Has a nice swim move
Tackling – He is an excellent tackler with good tackling range

Kenneth Grant is a mammoth defensive lineman from Michigan. He has excellent size, and his athleticism is unreal for his size. He also pairs that with excellent length. As a pass rusher, he is not very productive. I do like his bull rush and swim move if he gets one on one, but most of his style of play is run defense. He does a good job at being disruptive in the run game. He can move along the line well and has an excellent tackling range. He can improve his reaction time, as he sometimes reacts a little slow to pullers and open lanes. I love his strength in the run game, as he can take on double teams. He will be a good NFL player.
Hand Usage – He doesn’t use his hands as much as he should, could really gain more leverage if he used his hands properly
Pad Level – He often plays too high and loses leverage and control
Pass Rush – He does not offer much in that pass game, he can be disruptive but not especially productive
Read/React – He can be a bit slow on reading and reacting to run plays vs pass plays
Size – He is a massive human, and he can still add weight if he moves inside
Explosive – Jones is the definition of explosive, his get off is excellent
Effort – He gives some of the most effort I’ve seen, very high motor
Hand Counters – He does an excellent job at knocking down hands
Power – He has a lot of raw strength, and he can bring it out with power rushes and solid run defense

Sai’Vion Jones is a big, strong, long, and athletic defensive lineman from LSU. He played mostly edge rusher at LSU, but I like him playing a more inside role in the NFL. There is so much to like with Sai’Vion Jones, as he has excellent strength and effort, paired with elite explosiveness. He is a raw pass rusher, as he can work on using his hands and length more, but when he does use them, he is excellent. Against the run, he is solid. He has shown great anchor and strength but needs to work on his tackling. He will take a year or two to shift from an outside role to an inside role, but I can see him being a star D-Lineman in the NFL.
Use of Length – He doesn’t always use his length to the fullest advantage, needs to get his arms out more often
Inside Experience – He plays mostly an outside role, but I project him to play more inside, so he needs to get used to that technique
Pad Level – He plays a bit high in his pad level
Tackling – He does have a few concerning missed tackles, needs to clean that up before being an NFL force
Size – He is a very big dude
Athleticism – He is an excellent athlete for his size, very explosive
Penetration – He does an excellent job at getting into the backfield
Agility – His lateral agility is excellent; he moves from side to side super quickly
Violence – He plays with extreme explosiveness
Tackling – He is an excellent tackler with good tackling range

Joshua Farmer is a talented defensive tackle from Florida State. He has great size and length paired with amazing athleticism and agility. As a run defender, he can work on staying square and filling his gaps more effectively, but he does do a great job at getting penetration and making tackles. Due to his vertical quickness, he can rarely be blocked by pullers or reach blocks. As a pass rusher, he has a lot of upside. His pad level is consistently too high, but if he gets his hands down, he can be a violent pass rusher who can get pressure. I’d like to see him add more moves to his arsenal, but he will be a good DT in the NFL.
Gap Filling – He is more of a penetrating lineman rather than someone who can two-gap and fill their gap
Pass Rush Plan – He needs to gain more of a plan when rushing the passer
Pad Level – He plays with a very high pad level
Power – He doesn’t have overwhelming power with his bull rush
Hands – Needs to improve hand placement and counters
Size – He has excellent size for the position
Length – He has super long arms and he uses them really well against the run
Two-Gapping – He is a phenomenal two-gapper with his length and strength
Run Defense – He is a controlling, dominating run defender who moves people at will
Read/React – He is incredible at reading run plays, sees screens and counters very well

Alfred Collins is a big defensive tackle from Texas. He has excellent measurables and very solid athleticism for his size. As a run defender, he thrives. His film is littered with examples of him using his long arms to extend and throw offensive lineman out of the way to make tackles. He also reads and reacts to plays very well, consistently sniffing out screens. As a pass rusher, he lacks upside. He doesn’t have a strong bull rush and often rushes without a plan. He also has very low production. He is an interesting player because he is a master run defender but really won’t offer much on pass downs. I still like him as a run defender in the NFL.
Pass Rush – He pretty much has no pass rush upside, does not have production or motor in the pass game
Bull Rush – Despite his strength, he does not have a good bull rush
Pass Rush Moves – He does not have an arsenal of pass rush moves, no plan whatsoever
Explosiveness – His explosiveness is very good as a run defender but as a pass rusher, he seems to be totally zapped of explosiveness
Size – He is a big player, has a lot of mass, which makes him hard to move
Strength – He is extremely strong, rarely moved from his spot
Block Shedding – He is a fantastic block shedder, has a nice swipe move
Penetration – He does an excellent job getting penetration against the run
Gap Filling – Fills his gap consistently
Lateral Movement – Has good lateral movement

CJ West is a compact nose tackle from Indiana. He is shorter than most defensive tackles but is very compact and hard to move. His smaller size allows him to have natural leverage. As a pass rusher, he offers very little. He occasionally can catch offensive lineman off guard and shoot a gap but has very little production and effort against the pass. Against the run, he is a beast. He does a great job shedding blocks and consistently fills his gaps. He makes plays against the run and is very strong. He can work on his tackling and being less upright off the snap. He has starter quality potential at nose tackle in the NFL.
Vertical Explosion – He is not extremely explosive vertically, needs more drive
Pass Rush – He is not a pass rusher, has little to no production and seems to focus exclusively on run defense
Stands Up – He tends to stand up out of his stance, causing his pad level to get too high
Tackling – He can improve his tackling technique, often lunges at players
Agility – He is an extremely agile player, has great foot quickness
Quickness – Great first step and can win with quickness
Hand Counters – I like his hand usage, knocks down opponents’ hands well
Pass Rush Ability – He has the athleticism and pass rush IQ to be a good pass rusher
Block Shedding – When he actually engages, he is an excellent block shedder

T.J. Sanders is a pass rushing defensive tackle from South Carolina. Sanders has decent size, with room to bulk up some more. He displays excellent athleticism, especially laterally. As a pass rusher, he shines. His athleticism and hand counters give him sky high potential and disruptiveness. He is explosive and quick. As a run defender, he needs a little more work. When he engages and stays square, he is an excellent block shedder, however, he consistently leaves his gap or gets pushed out of it sideways and can’t make a play. He needs to be better at reading run plays. Overall, he has a lot of traits worth working with.
Run Fits – He can get pushed out of his gap relatively often, does not have great anchor
Squaring up – He often tries to win with quickness and does not square up to the defender against the run
Strength – Overall, he is not the strongest player in the class
Read/React – Leaves his gaps too often to try to make plays
Weight – He is on the lighter side for a DT, might need to bulk up
Explosiveness – He is extremely explosive out of his stance, very good start and stop ability
Hands – He has excellent use of his hands, does a great job at getting the lineman’s hand out of the way
Pass Rush Ability – He is an excellent pass rusher, wins in multiple ways
Block Shedding – He is an excellent block shedder
Athleticism – He is a super athlete

Omarr Norman-Lott is a violent defensive lineman from Tennessee. He never had a full time starter role at Tennessee, but he projects to a bigger role in the NFL. He has excellent size and athleticism for the position and plays with a violent temperament. As a pass rusher, he does a good job at using his hands to win and he has good athleticism and bend at the top of his rush. As a run defender, he is a good block shedder and can make plays, but he needs to be more consistent filling his gaps and reading the plays. Overall, I really think he can develop into an excellent defensive tackle, but he needs some more experience and development.
Snaps – He doesn’t play consistently on the defensive side of the ball, comes in situationally
Run Defense – He is typically not even in the game on run downs, but he struggles to hold his ground
Gap Filling – Needs to be more consistent when filling his gap
Consistency – He has played 5 years in college but has never had a consistent starter role or consistent production
Size/Athleticism – He has a good blend of size and athleticism for a nose tackle
Strength – He has INSANE strength, almost never loses even an inch of ground
Punch – He has a very strong punch, stuns the lineman
Two-Gapping – He is an excellent two-gapper, controls offensive lineman
Leverage – He uses excellent leverage to utilize his strength

Jordan Phillips is a monster nose tackle from Maryland. He is very young, at just age 20, and he has a lot of skills to work with. He has great size and decent athleticism for the position, although he is not especially agile. He plays nose tackle, so most of his positives come against the run, with excellent strength and an incredible ability to move offensive lineman at will. He lacks length but still wins with leverage and strength. He offers very little as a pass rusher, which will hinder his ceiling. He has a slower get off and needs to improve on his overall playmaking. He will be an interesting prospect but certainly has a role in the NFL.
Pass Rush – He has almost no pass rush plan and his production rushing the passer is basically nothing
Snap Timing – He has a slow get off because he does a poor job timing the snap
Playmaking – He needs to be more active in terms of playmaking, more tackles and more production
Length – He does not have great arm length for the position
Size/Athleticism – He is a very big dude who has excellent athleticism for his size
Explosive – He has excellent vertical explosiveness
Pass Rush Upside – He has an explosive bull rush and has the ability to capitalize with sacks
Versatility – He has played all over the defensive line
Pad Level – He plays with phenomenal pad level, getting low and gaining leverage

Vernon Broughton is an athletic defensive tackle from Texas. He has great size for the position as well as excellent athleticism. As a pass rusher, he shows off his traits. He has excellent vertical explosiveness, and he can make anything happen with his motor and great pad level. He is versatile but most likely will play 3-tech at the next level. As a run defender, he needs more consistency. He displays good strength and pad level, but he needs to refine his technique with gap filling and tackling. His instincts are also not elite yet, as he takes an extra second to diagnose plays sometimes. Overall, he has great potential at the position.
Pass Rush Plan – He needs a better pass rush plan, as he often just runs around or through people
Play Recognition – He can be a tad slow at times to diagnose plays and react
Gap Filling – He can get knocked out of his gap and miss his assignment
Tackling – He is not a great tackler, needs to finish better
Consistency – He needs more consistency in his production
Size – He is a mammoth of a man, one of the biggest Lineman ever likely
Length – He has extremely long arms, wins with length
Strength – He is very strong, especially with his hands, they pack a punch
Versatility – Has played nose tackle, 3-tech, and 5-tech
Hands – He has excellent hands, very strong and has a good swipe move

Deone Walker is a mammoth defensive tackle from Kentucky. He is a huge player with excellent length and strength. His athleticism is good for his size, but he is still slow at times. His motor is also questionable. As a pass rusher, he has a nice swipe move and displays good strength, but he is not consistent or athletic enough to be a pass rushing defensive tackle. He also has poor pad level due to his height. As a run defender, he does a good job at using his length and winning, however he can get stuck in blocks as he doesn’t shed them that well once engaged. Overall, he is a developmental player that has a role in the NFL.
Pad Level – Due to his height, he plays very high with his hands, loses leverage
First Step – He is not explosive out of his stance, is much lazier than he should be
Motor – He does not have a very hot motor
Pass Rush – He is not athletic enough to be a consistent force rushing the passer
Stuck in Blocks – He can get stuck in blocks and taken out of the play
Size – He is a huge player with an excellent base
Explosiveness – He is extremely explosive, especially vertically
Quickness – He gets off the snap really quick, displays good foot quickness
Strength – Can withstand double teams and win with strength
Run Defense – He has the ability to fill his gaps and make plays against the run, good penetrator

Jamaree Caldwell is a big and athletic nose tackle from Oregon. He is a huge player with excellent strength, especially in his lower body. One of his best traits is his get-off and explosiveness, as he plays with quickness and power at the same time. Against the pass, he can get pressures due to his quickness and power but needs to develop more of a plan and more moves to actually make a difference. As a run defender, he is good at being a penetrator and making stops but needs to be more consistent with stack and shedding. He also only has moderately good length. Overall, he has potential to be a dynamic nose tackle.
Pass Rush Production – Only one sack in 2024, which is concerning
Pass Rush Plan – He needs to have more of a plan than just running into players
Tackling – He can improve his tackling, had a 20% missed tackle rate in 2024
Block Shedding – He can struggle to shed blocks at times
Length – Has only moderate length, does not allow him to dominate
Explosive – He is very explosive, bursts out of his stance with speed and violence
Leverage – He has natural leverage due to his short stature
Pass Rush Upside – With his elite athleticism and good swim move, he has potential to be a very good pass rusher
Penetration – He is great at getting into the backfield
Hands – Strong, quick hands that are used well

Aeneas Peebles is a disruptive defensive tackle from Virginia Tech. He has a very short, stocky frame with below average length but elite athleticism. As a pass rusher, he displays an excellent swim move, a hot motor, and great leverage on his bull rush. He has potential to be an extremely disruptive pass rusher at the next level. As a run defender, he needs a little bit more work. He struggles to consistently fill his gaps. He lacks the length to two-gap, as well. He is a pure penetrator with elite athleticism. I think he can be a rotational defensive lineman to come in on pass downs and wreak havoc in the NFL.
Size – He is extremely small for a defensive tackle, short and light
Length – He lacks length, causing him to get caught up by longer tackles
Gap Filling – He often leaves his gap to try to get into the backfield instead
Tackle Range – He doesn’t have a great tackle range
Reliability – I have concerns about whether you can rely on him in the run game
Athleticism – He is an insane athlete for his size, displays good body control and explosiveness
Agility – He has excellent lateral agility, can move side to side very quickly
Pass Rush Potential – He has good pass rush potential with his athleticism and quickness
Size/Length – He has ideal size and length for the position, might need to add a couple pounds

Shemar Turner is a versatile but very raw defensive tackle prospect. He has ideal size and length for the position, and he pairs it with elite athleticism and quickness. He had poor production in 2024, but he has potential for good seasons in the future. As a pass rusher, he has an excellent first step and can win with his agility and length. I’d like to see him use his hands more and refine his technique. As a run defender, he needs lots of work. He is more of a disruptor but can’t hold his own against blockers. He is not a good block shedder and often gets pushed out of his gap. He will need some development, but in the future, he can be a pass rush specialist
Hands – He doesn’t use his hands well, doesn’t engage in the run game and doesn’t get them inside when rushing the passer
Production – He had poor production in 2024
Strength – He doesn’t have the strength to hold his own in the run game
Two-Gapping – He can’t two gap very well
Pass Rush Plan – He relies more on his athleticism to win, rather than technique
Size/Length – He is a massive human with excellent length
Versatility – Due to his size, he can play anywhere from 7-tech to 3-tech
Swipe – He has a very good swipe move, wins with it consistently
Heavy Hands – He has very strong, heavy hands that he needs to use more of
Run Defense – He is strong in the run game, does a good job at extending his arms

Jared Ivey is a strong tweener player from Ole Miss. He played a versatile role at Ole Miss, but at the NFL level I project him as a 3-4 DE. He has an excellent frame with insane length and a very strong lower body. As a pass rusher, he displays a good swipe move and heavy hands, but his pad level and his lack of explosiveness cause his bull rush and most other pass rush moves to be inconsistent and ineffective. His strength comes with his versatility and his run defense. He does a good job at setting the edge and he is strong and disruptive in the run game. I think he can have a role as a rotational 5-tech in the NFL.
Athleticism – He is unathletic, watching him move is taxing to look at
Agility – He has a very clunky movement style, not very agile
Tweener – He is a bit of a tweener in where he will play
Pass Rush – He needs to improve his pass rush ability overall, needs to add more technique and explosiveness
Motor – He does not have a high motor, gives up too often
Athleticism – He is a freak athlete who had success off the ball too
Bend – He has next-level bend, can get around corners quickly
Hands – He uses his hands very well, has good fakes and technique
Speed – He is an elite speed rusher, gets pressures super quickly
Disruptive – Is extremely disruptive in both the pass game and the run game, gets pressure consistently

Abdul Carter is a beast edge rusher from Penn State. He is a disruptive player and the type of player that you know will be an all-time great. His motor mixed with his explosiveness and hand usage makes him an unstoppable force at edge. He is a young player with only one year as a full-time edge, and he can improve on this already great base. He doesn’t have elite power or size, but he can still win with speed to power. In the run game, he is disruptive and plays the run with effort, but he has room to grow in his strength to hold his ground and in his tackling. His best trait is his incredible bend and quickness. He will be a superstar edge rusher.
Tackling – He is usually a great tackler, but he does have some missed tackles
Power – He does not have elite strength and power
Size – He is on the smaller side for an edge rusher, but I don’t think it will matter much
Explosiveness – He may be the most explosive player in the draft
Bend – He has excellent flexibility and bend around the edge
Motor – His motor is always hot, always looking for tackles
Speed to Power – He can convert speed to power with success
Attack – I love the way he attacks blocks
Arsenal – He has an arsenal of pass rush moves

Mike Green is an explosive rusher out of Marshall. He does not have elite measurables, as his length and size are somewhat lacking, however he is an elite pass rusher. He has an insane first step and can convert his speed to power or win with his arsenal of pass rush moves (my favorite was his spin against OSU). He has phenomenal bend to get around the edge and his motor is always hot. Against the run, I love how decisive he is and how he attacks blocks, but he needs to be more disciplined and better at diagnosing plays. He is someone that is just scratching the surface of how good he can be, even with 17 sacks in 2024.
Length – He does not have great length, will struggle more with longer tackles
Run Discipline – Needs to be more disciplined when setting edges and making decisions against the run
Competition Level – Playing at Marshall, does not get to show his ability against top tier players often
Size – He does look a little small for an edge, but it does not concern me because he plays big
Size – He has excellent size for an edge rusher, massive player
Athleticism – For his size, he has special movement skills
Strength – When he uses his bull rush well, it is effective, he is very strong
Agility – For his size, he has remarkable agility
Speed to Power – When he uses it, his speed to power can be deadly
Potential – Shows flashes of brilliance

Shemar Stewart is an intriguing watch from Texas A&M. He is a massive human with one-of-a-kind athleticism for his size. He flashes brilliance with speed to power, long arms, and spin moves, but he is so unproductive and inconsistent that it causes some concerns. He does not use his hands to win very often, and he doesn’t use his length well. Against the run, he plays with less urgency and his hands look much lighter. He doesn’t two gap or stay square very well. He has good agility and can be strong, but he needs to develop more of a pass rush plan to be an elite rusher at the NFL level.
Use of Length – He doesn’t use his length well, needs to work on using it better
Run Defense – He is not disruptive against the run, struggles to two-gap and stay square
Production – He was very unproductive in college
Plan – He needs more of a pass rush plan, does not use countermoves
Technique – He has very poor rush technique, runs down the middle of people
Explosiveness – He is an extremely explosive rusher, both in his feet and his hands
Length – He is very long, can still work on using his length
Agility – He has excellent movement skills and agility
Speed to Power – He does have the ability to rush with power
Bend – He has good bend and flexibility
IQ – Recognizes screens and motions well

James Pearce Jr is an uber-talented pass rusher from Tennessee. He has a solid frame but needs to add some weight to be a full-time rusher in the NFL. He has exceptional explosiveness off the line and great agility and length to win with his hands. He seems to have a good plan when rushing, however, he needs to work on countermoves if he gets stuck. He has great bend to get around the edge but struggles to tackle and finish sacks. As a run defender, he shows flashes of two-gapping and being disruptive, but he needs to be a more aggressive and consistent tackler. He also will need to add weight. Overall, he is an elite rusher.
Weight – He needs to fill out his frame as he is very light for an edge rusher
Counter-Moves – If he is stuck in a certain position, he often can’t get out
Aggressiveness – He needs to be more aggressive in the run game
Finishing/Tackling – He struggles to finish sacks and finish tackles in the run game, needs better technique and a stronger grip
Explosive – His movements are extremely sudden and explosive
Length – He is a lengthy player who uses his length well
Hand Usage – He has violent hands and uses them well, good hand placement
Run Defense – He is disruptive against the run and sets the edge well
Speed to Power – Translates speed to power well

Kyle Kennard is a tough pass rusher from South Carolina. Kennard has an explosive first step and everything he does after that epitomizes motor and effort. He has solid length and can use it well, as well as a solid frame for an OLB. As a pass rusher, he needs to work on having more of a plan and using more moves consistently. He does have a nasty inside move and he is extremely quick and twitchy in his rush. Against the run, he sometimes struggles to stay in his gap, but he is very disruptive and decisive in what he does. He struggles to diagnose run plays on occasions. He has had good production and can be a very solid rusher in the NFL.
Bend – He lacks a certain amount of bend around the edge, can’t flatten out at the top
Pass Rush Plan – I do think he can work on having more of a plan when he rushes, mostly goes down the middle
Block Shedding – He can work on getting off blocks, especially when trying to get around them
Diagnosing – Sometimes takes a second too long to diagnose a run or make a play
Size – He has a stocky, strong build, good for a defensive end
Production – He has been uber-productive at OSU for the past two years
Speed to Power – He gets a good bull rush and backs up the tackle
Run Defense – He sets the edge well and can two gap very well
Hand Placement – He gets his hands inside consistently, great on bull rushes

JT Tuimoloau is a stocky pass rusher from Ohio State. Tuimoloau is the definition of solid. Everything he does is very solid. He has excellent size and production, and he is very strong against the run. As a pass rusher, he is mostly a power rusher, utilizing hand placement and speed to power to win. He lacks an elite first step and struggles to speed rush in general. I’d like to see him develop more moves and more of a pass rush plan. Against the run, he is very strong. He can hold his ground and set the edge well and he stays square. He lacks elite athletic traits but will be a good player in the NFL.
Athleticism – He is not a spectacular athlete, is not very agile or quick
Pass Rush Plan – I’d like to see him have more of a plan, usually runs right down the middle of guys
Speed Rush – He doesn’t have a great first step or amazing bend at the top of his rush, relies on power
Arsenal – He doesn’t have a lot of moves and countermoves
Bend – Doesn’t have great hip flexibility
Motor – He is the definition of pure heart and motor, never stops churning his legs
Batting Passes – He consistently gets his hands up and bats passes
Hand Usage – I love his hand fighting ability, knocks down tackle’s hands
Leverage – He does a good job at getting low against players
Anchor – He has a strong anchor to hold his ground

Jack Sawyer is a solid pass rusher from Ohio State. He is the heart and soul of the Ohio State defense, and he has some solid traits. He has an excellent motor and displays top tier effort in the run game. He does struggle to overpower players and be disruptive, however. As a pass rusher, he has a subpar get-off and is not overly explosive. He does have the ability to rush with both power and speed, however, as he has excellent hand usage and decent bend around the edge. Despite his lack of athleticism, he is able to consistently make plays and an impact. He is also an excellent pass deflector. He will have a role as a very solid edge for an NFL team.
Athleticism – He is not an elite athlete, lacks some agility and quickness
Power – He doesn’t have overwhelming strength or power
First Step – He doesn’t have a very explosive first step
Staying Square – He can get sideways sometimes, especially in the run game
Twitch – In general he is not a very twitched up player
Speed – He is a pure speed rusher with excellent closing speed
First Step – Very twitchy player with an explosive first step
Bend – Has fantastic bend at the top of his rush, can finish well
Production – He is an extremely productive rusher, with 14 sacks in 2024
Finishing – He is a great tackler who rarely misses tackles and consistently finishes sacks

Donovan Ezeiruaku is a talented speed rusher from Boston College. He displays an explosive first step, mixed with excellent speed and an ability to consistently finish sacks. He is also extremely bendy at the top of his rush to get around the corner. He is undersized, which can lead to him getting taken out of lots of run plays. As a pass rusher, I’d like to see him develop more moves and a better speed to power rush. He needs to work on using his hands more when he rushes so that he is not a one trick pony. He will likely be exclusively a passing downs rusher in the NFL, as he is not good enough against the run to play all 4 downs.
Size – He is extremely skinny, does not look NFL size
Strength – He lacks much of any power, struggles to hold his ground in the run game
Hand Usage – He doesn’t win with his hands enough, relies on speed
Arsenal – He is a one trick pony with his speed rush
Run Defense – Does not hold up great against the run, needs to be better at holding his ground and setting an edge
Size – He has ideal size for an edge rusher
Length – He is extremely long, can get his hands on a tackle first
Strength – He is strong, can hold his ground in the run game
Athleticism – He is a good athlete, has solid speed and overall athleticism
Agility – He has good overall movement skills for someone his size, his ceiling is extremely high

Mykel Williams is a raw pass rusher from Georgia. At Georgia, he plays a lot of 5-tech and even some interior defensive line. He has excellent size for the position and insane length. He uses his length well, especially in the run game when he can control where he is due to his long arms. He does have issues with leverage as he goes too high and does not maximize his ability. He needs more of a plan as a rusher, and he does have elite explosiveness or quickness out of his stance. Due to his elite size and strength and solid movement skills, his ceiling is sky high. He is solid against the run and eventually can be a 3-down pass rusher.
Leverage – He consistently plays too high, causing him to lose strength on his bull rush
Pass Rush Plan – He needs to work on a plan when he rushes so he can use countermoves
First Step – His first step is slow for a rusher, cannot get the edge
Production – He has not been very productive, a raw prospect
Speed Rush – He doesn’t do a good job at getting around the outside
Size/Length – He has excellent measurables for the position
Explosive – He has explosive movements for someone of his size
Speed Rush – He has a solid speed rush, as he is very quick
Strength – Against the run, he displays good strength and anchor to set the edge
Motor – Wins a lot of reps by just not giving up and being consistent

Landon Jackson is a toolsy pass rusher from Arkansas. He has elite size and very good athleticism for the position. He also has excellent length and explosiveness. As a pass rusher, he is very raw. He has a solid get-off and is explosive in his movements, but he struggles to use his hands effectively. He doesn’t display a good bull rush and mostly wins with speed and motor. Against the run, he does show good functional strength and ability to set the edge, but I’d like him to be more disruptive at his size. He can work on his bend and his pad level in order to maximize his effectiveness as a pass rusher. He will have a role on an NFL team.
Pad Level – He is a taller prospect and plays a little too high at times
Hand Usage – He doesn’t use his hands enough, his hand placement is poor, and he gets stuck often
Speed to Power – He struggles to translate speed to power, needs better hand placement
Block Shedding – He is not an elite block shedder
Bend – He does not have elite hip flexibility and bend at the top
Size/Athleticism – He is a very big player but has good athleticism for his size
Speed to Power – He does a good job at converting speed to power
Quickness – He has a good first step and displays good quickness
Run Defense – Does a good job at staying square and setting the edge
Strength – He has good functional strength

Jordan Burch is a talented edge rusher from Oregon. Burch has great size for the position, and he pairs that with excellent explosiveness. As a pass rusher, he utilizes speed to power consistently but also has a great first step. He struggles as a speed rusher, as he has very poor bend and change of direction. I’d like to see him work on having more of a plan and being successful with finesse moves. He is an excellent run defender, as he is strong and keeps square with the defender. He has good functional strength for the position as well. He is not the longest, but he makes it work. Overall, he can be a really good compliment rusher in the NFL.
Bend – He has very poor bend and flexibility around the edge, struggles to flatten out
Pass Rush Plan – He plays without a plan for the most part, doesn’t have countermoves
Agility – He does not have great agility or change of direction
Pad Level – He tends to play a little higher than he should
Length – He does not have super long arms for someone his size
Quickness – He has a very good first step, explodes off the snap
Versatile – He plays at so many different alignments as well as off ball linebacker
Attacks – He doesn’t wait for pullers, he attacks them
Motor – He is an extremely high motor player, plays through the whistle
Athleticism – He is so explosive and has excellent athleticism at his size

Oluwafemi Oladejo is a twitched up pass rusher from UCLA. He has a compact frame and decent size for the position, as well as good length and great athleticism. As a pass rusher, he is extremely explosive. He plays with a red-hot motor and wins with effort. He needs to gain more experience rushing the passer, as he only has a half of a year. He needs to gain a better plan when rushing as well. As a run defender, he is very aggressive but can sometimes be too aggressive. He is a very raw player but has the right attitude and temperament to succeed in the NFL. I love him as a developmental player at an OLB position.
Pass Rush Plan – His plan is often to run through someone or go around, needs to add more moves
Strength – His overall strength is not elite, can work on holding ground against the run
Raw – He is very raw with his hand usage, needs to find more ways to win
Experience – He needs to learn how to play edge rusher better, only has half of a year playing full time edge
Explosive – He has explosive athleticism, very bursty
Speed Rush – His athleticism allows him to have a nasty dip and rip speed rush
Speed to Power – He has displays he can use speed to power effectively
Effort – He always gives high effort, even against the run and in coverage
Penetration – He does a good job on stunts getting penetration into the backfield

Kaimon Rucker is a high motor pass rusher from UNC. Rucker has a smaller stature but a compact frame. He has average length but has very good athleticism. As a pass rusher, he has a good first step and is very explosive in everything he does. He needs to expand his arsenal and gain more pass rush moves but he does have a nice dip and rip. He also does a good job at converting speed to power. As a run defender, he does a good job making plays but often looks to get in the backfield rather than filling his gap. He plays with violence and attitude. Overall, he needs to improve on some weaknesses but can be a productive player in the NFL.
Edge-Setting – He can work on setting the edge, especially in option situations
Versatility – He is only a stand-up pass rusher, doesn’t ever have his hand in the dirt
Size – He is a smaller edge rusher, very compact
Bend – Does not have elite bend despite his explosiveness
Pass Rush Plan – He needs to work on his arsenal, tends to run through people
Size/Length – He has a good frame with good length, weighed in at 264 at senior bowl
Bend – He has good bend around the edge, especially for his size
Production – He had 11 sacks in 2024, which is tied for best in the SEC
Speed Rush – Despite lacking elite explosiveness, he can get around the edge consistently
IQ – Diagnoses blocks well and does his job on trick plays

Princely Umanmielen is a gifted pass rusher from Ole Miss. Leading the SEC in sacks in 2024, he was extremely productive in college. He has ideal NFL size and length, and he has good athleticism to pair with it. He has an excellent speed rush, with great bend to get around the corner. He does lack an elite first step, and he seems to not have a plan when he rushes. When attempting to use power, he is less explosive than he could be. Against the run, I wish he would stay square more and be more disruptive, but he does a good job diagnosing blocks and tackling. He needs to clean up his technique to be a 4-down rusher in the NFL.
First Step – His first step is not very explosive, never gets a great jump off the snap
Pass Rush Plan – He looks lost when he rushes, needs to have a plan with countermoves
Speed to Power – He does a poor job at converting speed to power
Run Defense – He needs to stay squarer and be more disruptive against the run
Hand Usage – Needs to use his hands more
Size/Length – He has elite size and length for his position
Versatility – He can play up and down the line with his size and ability
Bull Rush – Has a very strong bull rush, good vertical drive
Run Defense – He does a good job at setting the edge and can stack and shed consistently
Tackling – He is a violent tackler
Strength – Very strong player, good lower body

Elijah Roberts is a strong edge rusher from SMU. He has excellent size and length but subpar athleticism for the position. He is extremely versatile as he can play multiple positions on the D-Line. As a pass rusher, he has a hot motor and excels in power rushing situations. He is a good finisher who will overwhelm with size and strength. He has poor agility and bend, making him a poor speed rusher. As a run defender, he is great at setting the edge and does a good job shedding blocks. He needs to work at tackling in open space, but he is a violent player who you want to run away from. He will be a strong player in the NFL.
Agility – His foot quickness is not very good, needs to work on his agility
Bend – He is not bendy at all at the top of his rush
Pass Rush Plan – Needs to rush with more of a plan, often just loiters on the edge waiting for an opportunity
First Step – Doesn’t have the timing down and is not quick off the snap
Space Tackling – Needs to work on tackling in space
Size – He is big and stocky, which allows him to be played at different positions
Long Arm – He has a very good long arm move that he uses a lot
Agility – His agility and movement skills for his size are exceptional
Arsenal – He has a good arsenal of moves, utilizes a long arm, spin move, and swipe move to win
Explosive – He is a very explosive athlete with a high motor

Ashton Gillotte is a really fun edge from Louisville. He has a stocky build and solid athleticism. As a pass rusher, he lacks an elite first step but is very explosive otherwise. He can convert speed to power, especially with his long arm move. He has a solid arsenal of pass rush moves but needs to work on counters. At the top of his rush, he does not have great bend. In the run game, he needs to work on his discipline and ability to shed blocks. He has a hot motor and great movement for his size. Due to his size profile, he may be a bit of a tweener, but I can see him working as a 5-tech if he works on his ability to shed blocks and hold his ground.
First Step – He does not have an elite first step, can be a tick slow
Bend – He lacks elite hip flexibility and bend to be able to get to the QB at the top of his rush
Run Defense – He is not very disciplined in the run game, can get ran out of his gaps
Block Shedding – He does struggle to get out of run blocks, needs to be more violent
Position – He might have trouble finding a starting role
Speed – He has a lightning fast get-off and he has excellent speed coming around the corner
Speed to Power – He has good leverage and does a good job at converting speed to power
Motor – He has an extremely hot motor, always moving
Explosiveness – He plays with suddenness and explosiveness
Violence – He plays with lots of violence, every move looks angry

Josaiah Stewart is a violent pass rusher from Michigan. At just 6’1, 248, Stewart plays with physicality and high effort to make up for his lack of size. As a pass rusher, Stewart has a quick first step and plays with excellent speed throughout the rep. He does not have great pass rush technique, as he needs to use his hands more in his rush. He has decent speed to power and can bend decently well, however. As a run defender, he plays with violence and explosiveness but ultimately might be too small to be a big factor in the run game. He will likely be a pass down rotational edge with a high motor and good athleticism.
Size – He is very small for an edge rusher, will be a concern
Technique – He doesn’t use his hands to win very much, needs to gain more moves and countermoves
Block Shedding – He struggles to escape blocks once tackles get hands on him
Strength – His overall strength is subpar
Run Defense – He will struggle against bigger players to two gap and play defense
Length – He is an extremely long rusher, uses his length well
Strength – Has a very strong upper and lower body, can bull rush very well
Size – He is a huge player, looks massive even lined up against big tackles
Hand Usage – I like the way he uses his hands, very strong and quick hands
Motor – He has a hot motor, always moving

Nic Scourton is a huge edge rusher from Texas A&M. He has a massive frame and excellent length for the position. Among his arsenal of pass rush moves, his rip move, and spin move stick out as his best. He also has a solid bull rush if he can get good leverage, which he needs to do more often. He has a hot motor and great strength. As a speed rusher, he lacks. He does not have a good first step and his closing speed and bend to finish a sack are lacking. Against the run, he is surprisingly movable, and I’d like to see him make more plays by shedding blocks. He has ok production but needs to do more to be considered elite.
Bend – Has really poor bend around the edge, cannot convert outside rushes into sacks
Speed – His closing speed and quickness is slow
Production – He has not been overly productive
First Step – He has a very slow first step, is not fast enough to win with speed
Gap Filling – Struggles to maintain his position against the run, not a disruptive run supporter
Speed to Power – He does an excellent job at getting into the tackle’s chest and forcing him backwards
Speed Rush – He has a good enough first step that occasionally he can win on the outside
Length – He is a long rusher
Motor – Does not give up on the play very often, always churns his legs
Athleticism – He is a good athlete who has showcased good change of direction

Bradyn Swinson is a lanky pass rusher from LSU. He has solid size for an OLB and has very good length for the position. He displays a good first step and great speed to power in his pass rushes. He does not have much of a plan when he rushes, however. He mostly tries to bull rush every time. I really like his motor and drive to get to the quarterback, but he needs some more moves to be more consistent. Against the run, he displays his athleticism and tackling prowess, but he is not strong enough to hold a good edge or be extremely disruptive. Overall, I think he is a really good rotational pass rusher with potential to become a starter in the NFL.
Pass Rush Plan – He seems to have no rush plan, as he consistently attempts to run down the middle of people
Run Defense – He is often not disruptive in the run game, does not do a good job at staying square
Hand Usage – He does not use his hands to win very often
Versatility – He is only a stand up pass rusher, can’t cover well
Strength – His overall strength is questionable
Hand Usage – He has  a nice swipe move and uses his hands a lot
First Step – He has a very explosive first step, can win right away with speed
Athleticism – Super athletic player
Agility – He has excellent change of direction while keeping his speed
Leverage – He has great leverage naturally, keeps himself low to win with power on occasions

David Walker is an athletic edge from Central Arkansas. He has poor size for the position as well as below average length. He is mostly a speed rusher, with his superior first step, his excellent agility, and his ability to finish. He does also boast good leverage and decent speed to power. He doesn’t have the strength I’d like to see in an edge rusher, and this hinders him when he is defending the run. He needs to expand his arsenal of pass rush moves and be better at using his eyes against the run. He plays against low competition, and the NFL will be a shock to him. Overall, he has a role as a potential rotational pass rusher.
Size – He is on the smaller side for an edge rusher
Competition Level – He plays against low levels of competition
Run Defense – He doesn’t have great eyes and often leaves his gaps or isn’t strong enough
Strength – Not the strongest player
Pass Rush Plan – He needs to rush with more of a plan, mostly runs around, inside, or through people
Speed – He has great speed for the position, is good in pursuit situations
Versatility – He played lots of different roles at Alabama
Speed Rush – He can win with pure athleticism and speed
Run Reads – He does a good job at reading runs and can defend fairly well against them
Leverage – He understands leverage very well, wins by getting inside and low

Quandarrius Robinson is an interesting study from Alabama. He plays a hybrid LB/Edge role for Alabama. He has a long, slender frame with great athleticism for the position. As a pass rusher, he has great speed and length but needs to refine his technique. He has shown a good long arm move and has shown he can convert speed to power, but that is about it. Against the run, he can make plays but often doesn’t have the strength to hold his ground long enough to be there. He makes more plays when playing as a spy, which he does often at Alabama. Overall, he is a developmental player who has potential in the future.
Size – He is extremely lean, looks too small to be an NFL edge
Pass Rush Moves – He needs to upgrade his pass rush arsenal, he lacks unpredictability
Strength – He doesn’t have the same level of strength as other rushers
Experience – He lacks experience, despite being a 5th year senior
Hands – Needs to get his hands on the lineman first or he loses the rep
Size/Speed – He has fantastic size and great speed for his size
Effort – Plays every rep at a high effort level, excellent in pursuit
Eyes – He has excellent eyes, good anticipation in coverage and against the run
Downhill – He is excellent at playing the run downhill
Movement – Fluid mover, good agility
Tackling – He is a strong tackler

Carson Schwesinger is an all-around linebacker from UCLA. He has good size for the position and excellent athleticism. He does have a little room to fill out his frame, however. He has great speed and good agility, which is displayed with his coverage ability. He has excellent eyes and instincts despite one year of starting experience. He plays the run exceptionally well, with great motor and tackling ability. He can deconstruct blocks decently well and plays best going downhill. He is very aggressive and can miss his fits sometimes, but he also makes lots of plays. Overall, I think he has a sky-high ceiling and a great floor in the pros.
Pass-Rushing – He is not a bad blitzer, but he isn’t as versatile and pass-rush savvy as some of the other LBs in this class
Experience – He only has one year of starting experience
Aggressive – He is aggressive in his reads, can get too aggressive and hopeful trying to make plays
Weight – Could add some weight
Athletic – He is an extremely fluid mover with great explosiveness
Speed – He has sideline to sideline speed
Versatility – He is extremely versatile, plays edge and LB
Blitzing – He is an excellent blitzer, very explosive and creative
Coverage – He is a good cover linebacker, does well in zone coverage
Tackling – He is an aggressive tackler with good technique
