Jihaad Campbell is an athletic freak linebacker from Alabama. He is very versatile, able to play both edge and all linebacker positions. He is a fluid athlete with good sideline to sideline speed. In coverage, he is athletic enough to cover anyone but can sometimes leave his assignment early. He is a fantastic, aggressive tackler. He plays at full speed at all times. He is a good blitzer as well, with 8 sacks in 2024. Against the run, he can get caught reacting too late to run concepts and he often struggles to maneuver blocks. He may need to add some strength to his frame. Overall, he is a plug and play WILL LB with potential in the NFL.
Weight – He is a lankier player, could stand to gain some more mass
Block Maneuvering – He struggles to get through blocks with consistency
Eyes – He is more of a reactor as opposed to an anticipator
Strength – He lacks elite strength
Jittery – He always wants to make a play, but sometimes he leaves his assignment too early to try and make a play
Athleticism – He is an athletic freak that will certainly test very well
Versatility – He plays lots of off ball linebacker as well as edge
Blitzing – He is an excellent, patient blitzer who can consistently get pressure
Motor – He has a hot running motor and is constantly moving towards the ball
Finishing – He usually does a great job at finishing the tackle or the sack

Jalon Walker is an athletic freak out of Georgia. He played both off-ball linebacker and edge in college and projects as a hybrid player for the NFL. He has excellent athleticism, with good bend and a hot motor, but he needs to work on his hand usage and overall technique. When rushing, he looks more like a blitzer just trying to get as far forward as possible, rather than focusing on winning the rush and making a play. He is a good tackler but needs to be smarter against the run. I don’t believe he has the size or strength to be a full-time edge and will likely need to develop and learn to gain a consistent role in the NFL, but his athleticism is elite.
Hands – He doesn’t use his hands to be lineman, uses only his athleticism and motor
Technique – He is someone who needs to be taught how to play edge, does not have a variety of pass rush moves
Run Disruption – He is not extremely disruptive against the run
Strength – Not a super powerful player
Size – He is on the smaller end for an edge, needs to bulk up
Versatile – He can play both edge and linebacker effectively
Athletic – Extreme athlete, is fluid and explosive
Blitzing – He is an excellent, patient blitzer who can consistently get pressure
Strength – He has held his own against the run with good strength
Playmaker – He is someone who, no matter where you put him, he can and will make plays

Jalon Walker is an athletic LB out of Georgia. He is extremely versatile and plays half of the time at edge and the other half at LB. He displays good, compact size for a LB, as well as decent length and fantastic athleticism. He is an absolute playmaker, whether he is blitzing or playing the run or in coverage. He is inexperienced, and his lack of experience causes him to be a little slow diagnosing run plays and route concepts. I would like to see him improve his pass rush technique to use his hands a little bit more. He can be disruptive against the run but needs to work on filling his gap. Overall, he is a project that can play all over.
Technique – He is someone who needs to be taught how to play edge, does not have a variety of pass rush moves
Run Defense – He is often not good at diagnosing run plays and is late to make plays
Coverage – He is not the most experienced player in coverage, often is slow to get his man
Gap Filling – Needs to work on setting the edge and filling his gaps with consistency
Size – He is a big player, very strong and built
Strength – He displays great functional strength against blocks
Downhill – He excels when he is tackling downhill, stonewalls players
Hit Power – He packs a punch when he tackles players
Run Defense – Defeats blocks and makes plays consistently
Explosive – He is an explosive athlete

Demetrius Knight Jr is a strong linebacker from South Carolina. He has great size and a strong build. He is an explosive athlete but is a little tight in his hips and has only average speed and agility. His strengths come with his ability to defend the run and generate pressure on the QB. He is very good at coming downhill and deconstructs blocks with good technique. He is a good tackler who hits hard. In coverage, he needs some work. He is not able to keep up with shiftier players. He can also work on angles he takes when in pursuit. He will likely have a WILL role in the NFL and he can be very good if he works on his mobility.
Agility – He doesn’t have the elite level of agility that many others in the class do
Angles – Occasionally he takes poor angles to ball-carriers
Coverage – He doesn’t quite have the speed and agility to be elite in coverage
Speed – Does not have top-end speed
Versatility – He may be limited in what he can do in the NFL due to poor change of direction
Size – He has excellent size, very big, strong frame
Athleticism – For his size, he has excellent mobility skills
Tackling – He is a very strong tackler who packs a punch when hitting people
Strength – Strong enough against offensive lineman
Downhill – Does his best work when tackling downhill, can meet RBs in gaps and stonewall them

Danny Stutsman is a big, athletic linebacker from Oklahoma. He has excellent size for the position, and he pairs it with explosive athleticism. He does lack a little bit of agility, but he certainly has adequate speed and athleticism to play LB. In coverage, he needs to work on his instincts and ability to cover in man. He thrives as a run defender, with excellent tackling and hit power, especially coming downhill. He has good strength and can take on blocks with force. He does need to show more playmaking ability, as he has had poor production in terms of INTs and sacks. Overall, he has a chance to start in the NFL.
Coverage – He is not elite in coverage, does not have the fluidity and agility to stay with shiftier players
Playmaking – He only had one sack and zero INTs in 2024
Agility – He does not have elite agility, can’t get to really shifty players
Instincts – He often misses his gap or coverage assignment due to poor instincts
Pad Level – Plays too high
Agility – He has excellent foot quickness, is very agile
Speed – He has sideline to sideline speed, can catch fast players
Blitzing – He is an effective blitzer, does a good job getting pressures
Coverage – He is good in coverage, can stay with TEs and RBs
Hit Power – He plays at full speed at all times, can create big collisions with good hit power

Chris Paul Jr. is an athletic linebacker from Ole Miss. He is a little small for the position but has room to grow out his frame. He is a great athlete, with excellent change of direction and true sideline to sideline speed. In coverage, he can stick with tight ends and running backs in man coverage and can make plays on the ball. He is an effective blitzer, with 14 career sacks. As a run defender, he can bring some pop when tackling players, but he needs to be more consistent with his run fits and needs to be better at block shedding. He can get stronger to help with this. Overall, he is a good player who has improved every year and can play in the NFL.
Size – He is small for a linebacker, might cause some concern
Gap Filling – He struggles to consistently fill his run fits
Strength – He is not the most built player, doesn’t win with strength
Block Shedding – He struggles to get out of blocks
Instincts – He is more of a reactor, struggles to anticipate directional changes or routes
Athleticism – He is a very athletic player, has great mobility skills
Versatility – He plays all over the linebacker core, Mike, Will, even edge
Speed – He has sideline to sideline speed
Tackling – He is a very strong tackler who doesn’t allow many extra yards to be gained
Agility – Great foot quickness and agility
Motor – He plays at full speed at all times, always running

Barrett Carter is a speedy linebacker from Clemson. He is a little small for the position but has excellent athleticism. In coverage, he can keep up with anyone with his speed and his incredible agility. He does need to work on contesting passes better, as his ball skills are poor. Against the run, his instincts are not great. He struggles to diagnose runs and isn’t great at getting off blocks. He is a strong tackler, and he can rush the passer with effectiveness. He is a versatile player who will be helpful on special teams due to his motor. Overall, I think Barrett Carter can be a linebacker eventually but will be a good special teamer.
Size – He is a smaller player for a linebacker, might need to gain some mass
Run Defense – He is very poor at diagnosing runs and being patient enough to meet the back in a gap
Block Shedding – Struggles to get out of blocks, doesn’t have great hands or strength
Ball Skills – Can stay with players, but needs to contest better
Strength – Not the strongest player
Movement Skills – He is a very fluid mover, good hips and good agility
Tackling – He is a consistent and good tackler
Coverage – He is decent in coverage, has the movement skills and eyes to be successful
Hand Usage – Takes on blocks strongly using his hands
Pad Level – He plays low and tackles around the legs, very consistent

Jeffrey Bassa is an athletic linebacker from Oregon. He is a smaller backer but has room to fill out his frame. He has great athleticism with decent speed and good fluidity. In coverage, he is able to stick with running backs and receivers, but his instincts in zone coverage are questionable. I’d like to see him make more plays. Against the run, I like the way he takes on blocks with his hands, but he doesn’t have the strength to stick against offensive lineman. He is a good tackler who gets low consistently. I’d like to see him work on his pass rush repertoire. Overall, I think he can be a developmental linebacker in the NFL.
Size – He is smaller for a linebacker, needs to bulk up his frame
Instincts – His instincts in zone coverage and when predicting run lanes are subpar
Strength – He lacks the necessary strength to take on blockers
Playmaking – He needs to make more plays consistently
Pass Rushing – Not an exceptional pass rusher, needs to gain some technique
Tackling – He has excellent tackling technique, minimizes extra yards
Block Shedding – Takes on blocks strongly and with his hands
Blitzing – He is a good blitzer, displays good pass rush ability
Special Teams – He has lots of special teams experience
Experience – He is a very experienced player, 6th year senior with lots of snaps played

Jack Kiser is an experienced linebacker from Notre Dame. He is a 6th year senior who has below average size and below average athleticism for the position. In coverage, he struggles to keep up with shiftier tight ends or running backs, and he is not a huge playmaker. His strengths come against the run, where his experience and tackling ability shows, as he has just a 4% missed tackle rate in 6 years! He takes on blocks well, but he is not the strongest player. He has lots of special teams experience and is also a good blitzer at times. He will likely be a special teamer for a long time in the NFL, but will mostly be a backup LB.
Size – He is a little small for a linebacker, not a big bruiser
Speed – Lacks top end speed to win in pursuit of ball carriers
Agility – His overall agility is not great, struggles to change direction
Read and React – He takes an extra second to diagnose plays and react
Coverage – He is not a great coverage player, struggles to stay with shiftier players
Athleticism – He is an elite athlete, has fantastic fluidity
Coverage Versatility – He can play press man and zone effectively
Ball Skills – He has excellent ball skills, finds the ball every time
Eyes – He has excellent eyes and play recognition
Mirroring – He does a good job at mirroring in man coverage
Tackling – He is a good tackler

Travis Hunter is a special prospect from Colorado. In addition to playing receiver, he also plays cornerback. As a CB, he displays elite movement skills and fluidity. He can move with anyone in college football. In man coverage, he has good, patient press technique with solid physicality and good mirroring technique throughout the rep. In zone coverage, he excels. His recognition skills are second to none and he has excellent ball skills to make plays on the ball. He is a little skinny for an outside corner, but I am not too concerned. Against the run, he could stand to get dirty a little more. Overall, he is a rare corner prospect.
Skinny – He is a skinnier player, looks much smaller than most of the receivers he plays against
Run Defense – He is not super involved in the run game
Hands – He has incredibly strong hands, makes catches with hands and not body
Ball Skills – He has incredible tracking and is always able to get the football
Athleticism – He is an elite athlete with excellent movement
Agility – Very agile player with good change of direction
Red Zone – He is an extreme red zone threat with his contested catch ability and ball skills

Travis Hunter is a supremely talented WR/CB from Colorado. As a receiver, he displays his top tier athleticism often, with crispy curl routes and quick crossers. He has secure hands and an excellent ability to find the ball and go up and get it. He is a danger in the red zone, as he consistently makes spectacular catches and gets open. I love his blend of athleticism and ball skills. He can work on some nuances in his game, such as his release or working on his route running further. After the catch, he can be a threat, but he doesn’t excel in that area. I would like to see him add ten pounds or so, as well. He will be a stud receiver in the NFL.
Weight – He is a little skinny for a wide receiver, might need to add 10 pounds or so
YAC Ability – He can continue to improve his ability to make people miss after the catch
Route Running – He is a smooth route runner, but his routes can be predictable
Nuances – I think he can work on some technical things such as his release and his ability to fake people out using his head and eyes
Size/Length – He has the ideal blend of size and length to be an outside corner
Physical – He is not afraid to make contact with people
Instincts – He is very instinctual, has fantastic eyes and acts on what he sees
Coverage Versatility – Can play both man and zone coverage
Ball Skills – He has very good ball skills, makes tons of plays on the ball

Will Johnson is a physical corner from Michigan. He has excellent size and length for the position and pairs it with very solid athleticism. In man coverage, he displays good press ability and physical defense throughout the rep. He lacks a little bit of closing speed but still makes plenty of plays on the ball. In zone coverage, he thrives when he can see the quarterback. He has good ball skills and instincts, but his change of direction can hurt him sometimes. As a run defender, he is ok. He is a strong tackler but needs to break down better and be more consistent. Overall, he will be a good corner in the league.
Tackling – He can improve his tackling, needs to work on breaking down and reacting
Agility – He doesn’t have the best agility, can get caught up sometimes by quick receivers
Speed – He doesn’t have elite speed
Aggressive – He is very aggressive, can be a little too aggressive at times
Athletic – He is a pure athlete, he can do so many things on the field
Playmaker – He has excellent ball skills and makes tons of plays on the ball
Versatility – Plays just about every position in the secondary
Eyes/Instincts – He is very decisive, closes in on what he sees with speed
Zone Coverage – He excels when he can see the quarterback and make plays

Jahdae Barron is a versatile defender from Texas. He has good size and length for the position as well as excellent athleticism. He is used all over the field at Texas and can play anywhere in the secondary. In man coverage, he has less experience. He doesn’t excel at press coverage and often can lose his man and be a little grabby. In zone coverage, he is excellent. He has fantastic instincts and eyes and great ball skills to make plays. In the run game, he is not afraid to get his nose dirty and make plays, but he needs to work on his block shedding. Overall, he is an excellent fit for a zone defense who will allow him to use his eyes and instincts.
Block Shedding – He needs to work on shedding blocks to make tackles on screens, runs, etc.
Press – He often plays off coverage or fades back from press, does not have a lot of press experience
Man Coverage – He is not the most experienced in man coverage
Grabby – He can get a bit grabby when he is in man coverage
Size/Length – He is a very lanky corner with good height and arm length
Speed – He has fantastic recovery speed, can make up ground with ease
Agility – Has excellent agility and ability to stop and start
Eyes – He has good eyes and instincts to where the QB is going to go
Ball Skills – He has excellent ball skills, always finds the ball and makes plays

Darien Porter is a long, athletic corner from Iowa State. He has great height and length for the position, as well as phenomenal athleticism. He is an older prospect, despite having limited experience starting at corner. In man coverage, he displays the ability to play press and shows his speed, as he can run with anybody. He has good agility and ball skills when the ball is in the air, but his hips are very tight, and he sometimes struggles to change direction. In zone coverage, he displays excellent eyes and instincts. IN the run game, he is physical but needs to be better at tackling. Overall, I think he is a hidden gem in this class.
Experience – He hasn’t been a full time starter until his redshirt senior season
Angles – He takes poor angles when tackling, needs to improve his tackling in general
Hips – His hips can be a little stiff, needs to work on flipping them
Production – only 4 PBUs and 3 INTs in his career
Age – He will be 25 by the end of his rookie season, possible concern
Size/Length – He has ideal size and length for the position
Athleticism – He is an explosive athlete who has excellent speed and explosiveness
Physical – He plays with good physicality
Zone Coverage – He does best when he can see the quarterback’s eyes
Press – He has shown the ability to play press coverage
Tackling – He is a strong tackler

Shavon Revel is a big, physical corner from East Carolina. He has an ideal frame with good length, strength, and excellent athleticism. He displays elite recovery speed and does everything with extra pop. In man coverage, he has shown he can play press and has good speed to stick on vertical routes, but his change of direction is subpar, causing him to be grabby at the top of routes. In zone, he does a good job reading the QB’s eyes but needs to work on his ball skills, as he has lots of drops and missed opportunities. He is a very strong tackler. Overall, if he can fix up some technique, he can be a top corner in the league.
Change of Direction – His agility and change of direction is solid for a bigger guy but he still needs to improve
Ball Skills – He has some drops and needs to turn his head more and look for the ball
Man Coverage – He is not as sticky as you’d like in man coverage
Injury – Had an ACL tear in 2024
Competition Level – Played at ECU, not many high level receivers played against
Press – He excels at mirroring players in press coverage and being physical
Physicality – Very physical player who loves to get hands on receivers
Man Coverage – He is sticky in man coverage
Vertical routes – He is very good near the perimeter where he can use his body to win
Ball Skills – He does a good job at making plays on the ball and not the player

Benjamin Morrison is a physical corner from Notre Dame. He has an average frame with subpar length and decent athleticism. He plays a lot of press man at Notre Dame, which he excels in. He has good mirroring technique off the line and does a good job at getting leverage on his man. His hips can be a little tight, but he makes plays on the ball with consistency. In zone coverage, he can be antsy and indecisive but still displays good ball skills. He doesn’t have ideal long speed, and his hip injury will be of concern, but overall, Morrison is a very physical player with a lot to offer a man-heavy NFL team.
Agility – He doesn’t have elite agility or change of direction
Speed – He seems to lack true top end speed
Instincts – His instinctual awareness does not impress me
Injury – He had a hip injury halfway through the season which could be detrimental
Hips – His hips can be stiff at times
Length – Doesn’t have elite length for a press man corner
Height/Length – He has good height and length for the position
Press – He is patient in press coverage and does a good job mirroring his man
Hips – He has very fluid hips, is able to flip them with ease
Ball Skills – Makes lots of plays on the ball, does a good job at using his length
Man Coverage – Does a good job at shadowing his man, has good athleticism

Trey Amos is an underrated corner from Ole Miss. He has good height and length for the position, as well as above average athleticism. He is a fluid player that can move with anybody. He does a good job in press coverage, and he displays good ability in man coverage. In zone coverage, he can be aggressive with his reads and his eyes but sometimes needs to dial it back. He has decent ball skills and does a good job at breaking up passes. He sometimes struggles to stop on a dime but mostly on curl routes. As a tackler, he can be more aggressive and improve his tackling technique. Overall, he will be a solid starting corner in the NFL.
Physicality – He could stand to be a little more physical when tackling and covering
Speed – He doesn’t have elite recovery speed, only average speed
Change of Direction – He struggles to start and stop on a dime, especially noticeable on curl and hitch routes
Run Defense – He is not a great run defender
Discipline – He likes to be aggressive with his reads, sometimes can be too aggressive
Physical – He is a very strong player and stays physical throughout the whole route
Tackling – He is an aggressive tackler who is not afraid of contact
Press – He does an excellent job at jamming players at the line
Ball Skills – He has elite ball skills and production, 7 picks in 2024
Man Coverage – He is good in man coverage, sticks with his man and makes life difficult

Nohl Williams is a physical corner from Cal. He has good size and strength for the position and is explosive. He is a prototypical man corner. He jams people at the line with consistency, sticks with them through the route and makes plays on the ball. He isn’t the most fluid mover, so he makes up for it by being a bit grabby. He has great ball skills and production, with 7 picks and 9 PBUs in 2024. He needs to work on being more disciplined in zone coverage, as he can be aggressive with his reads. He is a strong and aggressive tackler who is not afraid to help out in the run game. Overall, he has some really good traits that can be developed.
Aggressive – He is very aggressive in his reads, sometimes gets too aggressive and attacks a double move
Hips – His hips are a little stiff, struggles to flip them and change direction while keeping speed
Grabby – He is very grabby
Agility – He doesn’t have great agility, which he often tries to make up for with his physicality
Speed – Does not have elite speed
Speed – He has excellent recovery speed, nobody gets by him
Ball Skills – He does a good job at getting his head turned around
Press – He has good length and excels when he can play press man coverage
Zone Coverage – Does a good job at reading the quarterback’s eyes
Hips – He has very fluid hips, is able to continue his momentum without losing speed

Maxwell Hairston is a talented athletic corner from Kentucky. He has decent height and great length but is a little light for an NFL corner. He is also a phenomenal athlete. In press coverage, he displays good mirroring ability and good use of length, as well as good athleticism to keep with the receiver. He doesn’t have perfect technique in man coverage but gets the job done. As a zone coverer, he has great ball skills and a good ability to read the QB. He has good fluidity and speed, as well. He needs to get better at tackling and helping in the run game. He also needs to be more decisive in zone. He will be a starting corner in the NFL.
Size – He is a very skinny corner, might need to add some weight
Tackling – He is not a consistent and strong tackler, needs some work there
Physicality – He is not as physical as you would like to see from a corner
Explosiveness – He is not especially explosive or decisive, more of a fluid coverer than someone who will knock your socks off with explosiveness
Size – He is a bigger corner, good height and length
Physicality – He is a physical player who is not afraid to get hands on a receiver
Press – He has good mirroring technique and length for press man
Ball Skills – Does a good job to get his head turned around and find the ball
Run Defense – He shows a phenomenal willingness to tackle and be physical

Azareye’h Thomas is a big, physical cornerback from Florida State. He has good size and length for the position and displays decent athleticism for his size. In man coverage, he shows good ability to play press coverage and does a good job at getting his head around to break up passes. He lacks some change of direction and fluidity with his movement. In zone coverage, he is decent at reading the QB’s eyes but needs more turnovers. He does a good job at being physical but can be a bit grabby at times. Against the run, he is a very willing tackler but needs to work on his angles. Overall, he is a corner with starting potential.
Grabby – He can be grabby at the top of routes
Hips – His hips aren’t as fluid as I’d like them to be, needs to work on flipping his hips
Ball Production – Only 2 INTs in his 3 year career
Speed – He doesn’t have elite recovery speed
Change of Direction – He doesn’t change direction very well
Tackling – Can work on angles he takes when tackling
Height/Length – He is a lanky player with good height and length
Coverage Versatility – He has played lots of both man and zone effectively
Discipline – He has good discipline when playing zone, doesn’t bite for misdirects
Hips – He has fluid hips, flips them well and keeps his speed
Ball Skills – He has good ball skills, gets his head around and uses length well

Dorian Strong is a long, tall corner from Virginia Tech. He has good height and height but might need to add some weight in the NFL. He has good athleticism but not fantastic recovery speed. He can play press but needs to be a little more physical on the line. In man coverage, he displays fluid hips and good ball skills but needs to keep himself lower to change direction easier. In zone coverage, I like his eyes and the choices he makes. Against the run, he needs a lot of work. He can’t get off blocks well and struggles to be physical against bigger players. He is not an awful tackler but needs some work. Overall, he is a developmental corner.
Skinny – His weight may be a concern, as he is very lean and lanky
Run Defense – He struggles to get off blocks and is not much of a help against the run
Speed – He does not have good recovery speed, if he falls behind, he struggles
Grabby – He can be grabby downfield
Man Coverage – He is not a natural man cover corner, struggles to stay with receivers at times
Physicality – He is an extremely physical corner, puts hands on people
Run Defense – He is a willing run defender who is not afraid to get his nose dirty
Press – He does a great job jamming players at the line, good use of hands
Eyes – Has good eyes for who is open and who needs covered
Versatility – Is a versatile player who can play man or zone

Denzel Burke is a physical corner from Ohio State. He has average size and length for the position but is a very good athlete. He is an excellent press corner, as he does a great job jamming receivers at the line. He excels when he can be physical and aggressive. He sometimes gets too aggressive and goes for the INT when he shouldn’t. He has middling speed and fluidity but stays with the receiver. When the ball is in the air, he struggles to locate it and make plays. He can play both man and zone but is better in man. As a run defender, he is aggressive and a decent tackler. Overall, he has starting potential in the NFL.
Ball Skills – Struggles to locate the ball in the air and doesn’t have particularly great playmaking ability
Speed – He does not have elite recovery speed
Aggressive – He can be aggressive in his reads and may leave someone else open
Hips – He has tight hips, struggles to change direction at times
Production – Does not have a lot of INTs in his career
Physical – I like his physicality and how he always gets his hands on the receiver early in the route
Run Defense – He is willing to tackle and give effort against the run
Press – He excels when he can get his hands on the receiver early
Tackling – He is a good tackler
Versatility – Has experience playing both outside and inside as well as man and zone

Jacob Parrish is a physical corner from Kansas State. He is a little bit small and doesn’t have elite length for the position, but he is a good athlete. He is a versatile player who can play outside or inside but likely projects inside at the next level. He is a good press corner who thrives when he can get his hands on the receiver. He isn’t the most fluid player and struggles at the top of routes with being too conservative, however. In zone, I’d like to see him trust his instincts more and make more plays. He is a strong tackler who is willing to play the run. Overall, he is a versatile DB who has a chance to eventually start in the NFL.
Size – He is a smaller corner, may have to play inside at the next level
Hips – He doesn’t have the most fluid hips, struggles to completely flip them
Conservative – He lacks elite instincts and aggressiveness in zone
Top Of Routes – Often struggles to keep with the receiver at the top of routes
Ball Production – He is not much of a playmaker
Size/Length – He has good size and compactness, good length
Contact – He is very aggressive, not afraid to hit players
Versatility – He is very versatile, can play inside and outside
Fluidity – He has great movement skills, very fluid hips and good change of direction
Ball Skills – He has great production and very good ability to find the ball in the air

Quincy Riley is a fluid corner from Louisville. He displays average size and decent length for the position, as well as great athleticism. As a man coverage corner, he does a great job. He presses decently well and displays good fluidity and ball skills when covering players. He has had good production in his career and is a versatile player who can play inside and outside. In zone coverage, I need to see him trust his eyes and instincts more, as he can be hesitant. He also needs to work on his run defense and tackling, as he takes poor angles to the ballcarrier. Overall, he can be a good depth corner in the league with some potential.
Speed – He has lower top end speed than what I would like to see
Zone Coverage – He is not the most instinctual player, can be indecisive in his reads
Hesitation – I would like to see him be more decisive
Tackling – He takes poor angles to the ballcarrier and can often let people go by
Age – He is an older player, will be 24 when he starts his rookie season
Height/Length – He is very tall and has great length
Eyes – He has very good eyes in zone coverage, displays good instincts
Ball Skills – Tracks the ball very well and uses his length to make plays
Playmaker – Has 12(!!) picks in his career at Kansas
Coverage Versatility – He has the ability to play man and zone
Physical – He is a dawg, plays every snap hard

Mello Dotson is a long, lanky corner from Kansas. He has great height and length for the position but is an average athlete. Dotson is a versatile corner who can play man or zone relatively effectively. He is not the most fluid player, and he doesn’t have great recovery speed, but he can play man coverage decently well due to his positioning and physicality. As a zone corner, he thrives. He has excellent ball skills and eyes to make plays in zone coverage. He shows good effort against the run, despite not being the strongest or most refined tackler. Overall, he is a developmental corner who has starter potential in the NFL.
Run Defense – He isn’t great at shedding blocks and needs to get better at tackling
Speed – He lacks elite recovery speed, can get caught behind people at times
Fluidity – He is not a very fluid mover, needs to work on flipping his hips
Discipline – He can get a bit aggressive when playing zone
Tackling – Can refine his tackling technique
Height/Length – He has good height and length for a corner
Agility – Despite his lankiness, he still is able to change direction well
Ball Skills – He has excellent ball skills, has great production as well, with 4 picks and 4 PBUs in 2024
Production – 13 INTs in his 4 year career at Kansas
Aggressive – Can be seen as a weakness, but he always goes for the play, never is conservative

Cobee Bryant is a playmaking corner from Kansas. He has good height and length for the position, but he is very light and is not an elite athlete. He struggles in man coverage, as he doesn’t have the fluidity or press technique to be effective as a shadow. He does not have top tier speed, either. As a zone corner, he is better. He does have some problems with eye discipline, but he is a true playmaker. He is aggressive in his reads and uses his excellent ball skills and length to make plays consistently. Against the run, he needs some work as he is very light and has poor tackling technique. Overall, his playmaking ability will get him drafted, but he needs time.
Press – Doesn’t have great technique in press coverage, needs to use his hands better
Speed – He does not have elite speed to stay with fast receivers
Weight – He is very lanky and light, needs to add some strength
Man Coverage – He is not an excellent man cover player, struggles to stay with his man
Run Defense – He has poor tackling technique and is not strong enough to play the run
Height/Length – He has good height and length for the position
Instincts – He has really good instincts in zone coverage, always knows who is in what position and where they are going
Tackling – He is a relatively sound tackler
Ball Skills – Does a good job locating the football and makes plays on the ball
Physicality – He plays physical football, not afraid of contact

Zy Alexander is a long, tall corner from LSU. Zy has great height for the position and good length as well. He is only an average athlete but displays good physicality. He plays mostly off-coverage at LSU and, when asked to play press, struggles due to his stiff hips and poor technique. He is certainly more of a zone corner, where he can use his instincts and ball skills to make plays. He is a physical player who can be of help in the run game as a good tackler, but he needs to add more weight and strength. He can make some mistakes and has a lot of work to do as a coverage corner. He is a developmental player in the NFL.
Feet – He doesn’t have super quick feet, can get caught out and becomes grabby when he is uncomfortable
Skinny – He is very lean and light, may be a concern at the next level
Hips – He is not a fluid mover; his hips are a little stiff and he struggles to change direction
Man Coverage – He is more of a zone corner
Press – Plays much more off-coverage, struggles in press
Size/Athleticism – He is a big safety and has excellent athleticism for his size
Range – He can be a true deep safety, with his speed on the backend
Physicality – He is not afraid to be physical in run defense and coverage
Tackling – Has a career missed tackle rate of 2.2%
Long – He has an excellent tackle radius and a good catch radius for a safety

Kevin Winston Jr is a raw safety prospect from Penn State. He has excellent size for the position, and he pairs it with fantastic athleticism, especially explosiveness. In coverage, he could use a little work, as he is not as anticipatory as you want in a safety; he doesn’t have a lot of ball production. He is fluid and has good athleticism to stay with players in coverage. Against the run, he shines. He has excellent tackling technique, and his burst allows him to hit hard coming downhill. He is very long with good tackle radius. If his medicals check out, he will be a very highly selected safety in the NFL draft.
Injury – He missed the entire 2024 season due to a torn ACL
Production – He only has one year of really solid production, only one career INT and under 70 career tackles
Aggressive – Occasionally he can get too aggressive when coming downhill
Anticipating – He doesn’t anticipate passes that well
Coverage – Needs to work on his pure coverage abilities
Size/Athleticism – He is a freak athlete, and he has excellent size; one of a kind athletic profile
Speed – He has a crazy top speed, long strider
Versatility – He has taken extensive snaps as a box safety, free safety, and nickel
Tackle Radius – He is very long and can make tackles anywhere
Hit Power – He can hit like a truck when coming downhill, not the person you want to see in the hole

Nick Emmanwori is a freak safety from South Carolina. He has elite size for the position, and he pairs it with a unicorn athletic profile. He has excellent top speed and is explosive coming downhill. He does have some agility concerns, as his hips are quite stiff, but he makes it work. In coverage, he has fantastic ball skills but can work on reading plays and reacting quicker. Against the run, he is like a train coming downhill, he does not stop until he hits his destination. He has a fantastic tackle radius and is very versatile. Overall, if he has some more experience, he can be one of the better safeties the game has seen.
Man Coverage – He can still work on his man coverage ability, not quite as fluid and quick in man
Instincts – He is not quite as instinctual of a player as I want in a safety
Hips – He doesn’t have super smooth hips, long legs
Read and React – Doesn’t react quickly enough in zone coverage
Agility – Not the most agile player, can get beat by shifty guys
Versatility – Can line up in lots of spots, has the size and athleticism to play anywhere
Instincts – He always has a good idea of what is going on around him, quick reactor
Athleticism – He is an excellent athlete with good twitch and speed
Coverage – He is fluid in coverage and makes plays on the ball
Responsibility – He is the leader of the Georgia defense, plays everywhere

Malaki Starks is a versatile safety from Georgia. He can play anywhere but will likely be a free safety/slot mix in the NFL. He has adequate size and great athleticism for the position. He is the leader of the Georgia defense, and he excels at being around the ball at all times. He is a very instinctual player who is good in coverage but can occasionally let up some plays when lined up against good route runners. Against the run, he displays good instincts and a nose for the football, but he is not as strong of a tackler as I’d like him to be. He isn’t asked to blitz a lot, and he doesn’t do too much when he is. Overall, he is a talented defender.
Route Runners – He can improve on his man coverage abilities, not quite good enough at shadowing good route runners
Physicality – I’d like to see him be MORE of a missile, doesn’t play at full speed at all times
Tackling – He is a decent tackler, but needs to be stronger in his tackles
Blitzing – He is not an overly effective blitzer
Regression? – Played better in 2023 than 2024
Route Recognition – He has excellent route recognition skills, regularly jumps routes
Range – He has good speed on the backend, can go sideline to sideline
Instincts – He has very good instincts
Coverage – He has excellent athleticism and ability to stay with receivers in coverage
Ball Skills – He has excellent ball skills and production, 5 interceptions last year

Andrew Mukuba is a ball hawking safety from Texas. He has a very lean frame at only 5’11, 186 lbs, but he has some excellent athletic and mental traits. In coverage, he is excellent. He can play man or zone and has the agility and athleticism to stay with anyone. He also displays excellent ball skills to make plays on the ball. His instincts really shine in zone coverage. As a run defender, he is not elite. His small frame offers less hit power than other safeties and he can improve his tackling technique. He does have the effort there to play the run. He is also very fast. Overall, I believe he can start right away at free safety.
Size – He is a bit small for a safety, may need to add some weight
Versatility – He is almost exclusively a free safety, with limited snaps at slot and in the box
Block Shedding – He can get knocked around a little bit by bigger players
Tackling – He can improve his tackling technique
Playmaking – He is an excellent playmaker, 13 career interceptions
Effort – He plays at 100% motor at all times, plays the run and the pass with max effort
Instincts – He is a very instinctual player who reacts quickly
Ball Skills – He has excellent ball skills
Burst – He plays with excellent short-area burst
Smart – Jumps routes routinely

Xavier Watts is a talented safety from Notre Dame. He has adequate size and decent athleticism for the position. In coverage, he displays excellent play recognition and instincts to jump routes and fantastic ball skills to make plays on the ball. He is lacking a little bit of fluidity and speed to play against receivers, but he can cover tight ends and running backs. As a run defender, he displays elite short area burst to get downhill, and he always plays at 100% effort. He can work on shedding blocks and being a more consistent tackler. He likely will be a free safety in the NFL and can be a good, ball hawking one if they use him right.
Athleticism – While he certainly is not a bad athlete, he doesn’t have special fluidity and agility
Angles – He occasionally takes poor angles in pursuit of the ballcarrier
Block Shedding – He can get caught up in blocks and get taken out of plays
Tackling – Has a 13.5% missed tackle rate, needs to improve his technique
Range – Doesn’t have elite speed
Size/Athleticism – He has excellent size for the position and is athletically gifted
Downhill – He comes downhill with some explosive burst
Blitzing – He is an effective blitzer, 13 pressures in 2 years
Aggressive – He is extremely aggressive, jumps routes and run plays
Versatility – He has the athleticism and attitude to play anywhere in the secondary

Jonas Sanker is an explosive safety from Virginia. He has good size for the position and also displays excellent athletic traits. He projects as a strong safety at the next level. In coverage, he displays good athleticism to stay with the receiver, but he doesn’t have the playmaking skills to make plays on the ball consistently. He also lacks some fluidity in his hips. As a run defender, he brings an aggressive downhill presence. He displays good ability to avoid blocks and make hard hits. He does need to work on his angles that he takes to the ballcarrier. Overall, he has the skills to be an above average safety in the league.
Hips – He doesn’t have elite fluidity, can get caught in coverage on quick change of direction routes
Angles – He takes poor angles to the ballcarrier, needs to dial back his aggressiveness
Playmaking – He only has 2 career interceptions, not a ball-hawk
Deep Safety – I don’t love his skillset at deep safety, he translates more as a box safety
Versatility – Plays lots of different positions, mostly at free safety
Size/Athleticism – He has good size and is a good athlete for the position
Physicality – He is not afraid to get dirty and m make tough tackles
Run Defense – He does a good job against the run, makes tackles and diagnoses plays well
Blitzing – He blitzes really well, shows natural ability to get pressures

Lathan Ransom is a well-rounded safety from Ohio State. He has good size and athleticism for the position. He played lots of free safety but projects to strong safety in the league. As a run defender, he excels. He is great at coming downhill and has good hit power and ability to diagnose run plays. He can cut down on his missed tackles, however. In coverage, he struggles a bit more. He doesn’t have elite agility and fluidity in coverage, and he often gets really grabby. He is a good blitzer, with 13 career pressures and 3 career sacks. Overall, Ransom is a talented strong safety who can make a big impact in the run game but needs work.
Man Coverage – He struggles heavily in man coverage, doesn’t have good mirroring technique, gets very grabby
Agility – His overall change of direction and agility is subpar
Missed Tackles – Needs to cut down on his missed tackles, 16.7% career missed tackle rate
Instincts – Is not as quick of a reactor as you’d like in a safety, especially in coverage
Agility – He has cat-like footwork, super quick and light on his feet, can change direction in a flash
Speed – He has great speed to keep the backend from being broken
Ball Skills – He has good ball skills, 11 career interceptions
Read and React – He is a very quick reactor
Versatility – He plays all over the field, including free safety and nickel

Billy Bowman Jr is a versatile safety from Oklahoma. He is quite small for the position, and he has poor length, which leads to him being outmatched by bigger guys. In coverage, he displays blazing speed, cat-like agility, and fantastic ball skills. He can play man or zone and make plays on the ball. Against the run, he displays good burst coming downhill, as well as quick reaction time, but his lack of strength and poor tackling technique can lead to disaster. He plays a mix of free safety, box, and nickel but I project him as a nickel at the next level. He needs to work on his tackling, but he can be a viable starter for an NFL team.
Size – He is a very small safety, only 5’10, 192
Strength – He lacks ideal strength for a safety, can’t stonewall players
Block Shedding – He struggles to escape blocks, gets enveloped
Tackling – He has a whopping 25% missed tackle rate, needs to refine his technique
Length – He doesn’t have great length, leads to a poor tackle radius and a worse catch radius
Athleticism – He is extremely athletic, very fast and very quick
Speed – He can stay with just about anyone in coverage
Versatility – He plays lots of positions in the secondary, mostly nickel
Burst – He comes downhill really quickly against the run
Instincts – He has good instincts, jumps routes very often

Upton Stout is a small but feisty nickel from Western Kentucky. He has a very small frame and not a lot of length, but he plays with excellent burst and speed. He is a versatile player who plays all over for WKU but will likely find a home in the slot. He has good coverage ability with good fluidity and agility. He also displays feisty ability in the run game. He has good downhill burst and is a decent tackler. There are concerns with his injuries and his competition level, but he has the skills to excel. Overall, I think he will likely be a special teams contributor in the NFL.
Size – He is very small which might force him to play exclusively nickel at the next level
Competition Level – At Western Kentucky, he doesn’t play the top levels of competition
Strength – He doesn’t have elite levels of strength
Length – Doesn’t have elite length to make tackles or interceptions
Injury – He has had lots of injuries in his college career
Compact – He has a compact frame, is strong and low to the ground
Versatility – Has played multiple positions, mostly in the slot
Burst – His ability to burst downhill on runs and screens is excellent
Hips – He has nice, fluid hips in coverage to stay with the receiver
Ball Skills – He has good ball skills to make plays on the ball
Run Support – Helpful against the run

Sebastian Castro is a versatile nickel defender from Iowa. He plays lots of positions but is mostly a slot corner. He has decent, compact size but is not an excellent athlete. He lacks the long speed to stay with vertical routes and his agility is subpar in short areas. In coverage, he displays fluid hips and good ball skills but lacks length. He excels as a run defender, where he can burst downhill and make strong tackles. He does need to cut down on his missed tackles as he misses too many. He is an older prospect, but I think he can make an immediate impact as a nickel defender who specializes in run defense.
Speed – He doesn’t have elite range, sometimes struggles to stay with receivers
Missed Tackles – He has to cut down on his missed tackles, as he has a 16.2% career missed tackle rate
Agility – He has below average foot quickness, needs to improve agility
Length – Doesn’t have great catch radius or tackle radius
Age – He will be 25 by the start of his rookie season
